body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>,
Homage

body.text:
śāstrasyāsya praṇetāram abhyarhya sugatātmajaṃ [/]
vaktāraṃ cāsmadādibhyo yatiṣye 'rthavivecane //
body.translated_text: Having duly revered the composer of this treatise, the son of the Well-Gone One (<s>Sugata</s>), I shall endeavor, for speakers beginning from ourselves, in the discrimination of the meaning,
Body of the Treatise
Here, to begin with, the body of the treatise is established,

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ hy āvṛtis tatvaṃ pratipakṣasya bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: For definition, indeed, is the characteristic; the reality; the cultivation of the antidote,

children.text: tatra ca sthā phalaprāptir yānānuttaryam eva ca //
children.translated_text: And herein also the stages, attainment of the result, and the unsurpassed of the vehicles as well,

body.text: ity ete saptārthā hy asmiṃ cchāstre upadiśyante / yad uta lakṣaṇaṃ āvaraṇaṃ tatvaṃ pratipakṣasya bhāvanā / tasyām eva ca pratipakṣabhāvanāyām avasthā phalaprāptiś ca yānānuttatyañ ca saptamo 'rthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus these seven topics in this treatise are taught: that is to say, definition; obscuration; reality; the cultivation of the antidote; and precisely within that cultivation of the antidote, the stages; and attainment of the result; and the unsurpassedness of the vehicles as the seventh topic,
CHAPTER I. Section on Definitions
1. <s>Abhūtaparikalpa</s> (imaginary construction); a. the mark of existent and non-existent
Thereupon, beginning with the definition, he states:

children.text:
abhūtaparikalpo 'sti dvayan tatra na vidyate /
śūnyatā vidyate tv atra tasyām api sa vidyate // 1.1
children.translated_text: <s>Abhūtaparikalpa</s> (imaginary construction) exists; duality is not found there, emptiness is indeed found here, and even within that it is found, 1.1

body.translated_text: Mvbh 18

body.text: tatrābhūtaparikalpo grāhyagrāhakavikalpaḥ / dvayaṃ grāhyaṃ grāhakañ ca / śūnyatā tasyābhūtaparikalpasya grāhyagrāhakabhāvena virahitatā / tasyām api sa vidyata ity abhūtaparikalpaḥ / evaṃ yad yatra nāsti tat tena śūnyam iti yathābhūtaṃ samanupaśyati yat punar atrāvaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati tat sad ihāstīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīty aviparītaṃ śūnyatālakṣaṇam udbhāvitaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Here, <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> is the conceptual construction of grasped and grasper; the duality is the grasped and the grasper; emptiness is the absence, with respect to that <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, of the status of grasped and grasper; even within that, it is found—this is <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>. In this way, he sees in accordance with reality that whatever is not present in a given locus makes that locus empty by that [absence], and he understands in accordance with reality that whatever remains here is truly present—thus the unperverted mark of emptiness is brought to light,

children.text:
na śūnyaṃ nāpi cāśūnyaṃ tasmāt sarvaṃ vidhīyate /
satvād asatvāt satvāc ca madhyamā pratipac ca sā // I.2
children.translated_text: It is not empty, nor is it non-empty; therefore everything is designated; from existence, from non-existence, and from existence—this is the middle approach, I.2

body.text: na śūnyaṃ śūnyatayā cābhūtaparikalpena ca / na cāśūnyaṃ dvayena grāhyena grāhakeṇa ca / sarvaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ cābhūtaparikalpākhyaṃ / asaṃskṛtaṃ ca śūnyatākhyaṃ / vidhīyate nirdiśyate satvād abhūtaparikalpasya asatvād dvayasya satvāc ca śūnyatāyā abhūtaparikalpe tasyāṃ cābhūtaparikalpasya sā ca madhyamā pratipat / yat sarvaṃ / naikāntena śūnyaṃ naikāntenāśūnyaṃ / evam ayaṃ pāṭhaḥ prajñāpāramitādiṣv anulomito bhavati sarvam idaṃ na śūnyaṃ nāpi cāśūnyam iti /
body.translated_text: It is not empty—neither by emptiness nor by <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>; nor is it non-empty—by the duality of grasped and grasper. Everything conditioned is what is termed <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, and the unconditioned is what is termed emptiness; it is designated—pointed out—on account of existence, of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>; of non-existence, of duality; and of existence, of emptiness, within <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, and of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> within that—this is the middle approach with respect to all things: not exclusively empty, not exclusively non-empty. In this way, this reading is harmonized with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and similar texts: “All this is not empty, nor again non-empty,”
b. Own-characteristic

body.text: evam abhūtaparikalpasya sallakṣaṇam asallakṣaṇaṃ ca khyāpayitvā / svalakṣaṇaṃ khyāpayati /
body.translated_text: Having thus made known the existent and non-existent marks of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, he makes known its own-characteristic,

children.text:
arthasatvātmavijñaptipratibhāsaṃ prajāyate /
vijñānaṃ nāsti cāsyārthas tadabhāvāt tad apy asat // I.3
children.translated_text: A seeming of object, existence, self, and cognition arises; and the cognition does not have that object, because of the absence of that—hence that too is non-existent, I.3

body.text: tatrārthapratibhāsaṃ yad rūpādibhāvena pratibhāsate / satvapratibhāsaṃ yat pañcendriyatvena svaparasantānayor [/] ātmapratibhāsaṃ kliṣṭaṃ manaḥ / ātmamohādisaṃprayogāt / vijñaptipratibhāsaṃ ṣaḍ vijñānāni [/] nāsti cāsyārtha iti / arthasatvapratibhāsasyānākāratvāt / ātmavijñaptipratibhāsasya ca vitathapratibhāsatvāt /

children.translated_text: Mvbh 19

children.text: tadabhāvāt tad apy asad iti / yat tadgrāhyaṃ rūpādipañcendriyaṃ manaḥ ṣaḍvijñānasaṃjñakaṃ caturvidhaṃ tasya grāhyasyārthasyābhāvāt tad api grāhakaṃ vijñānam asat /
children.translated_text: Thus, “because of the absence of that, that too is non-existent”: since what is grasped—form, the five senses, and mind—and what is termed the six cognitions are fourfold, because of the absence of that grasped object, that which grasps, cognition, is also non-existent,

body.translated_text: Here, “seeming of object” is what appears in the mode of form and so on; “seeming of existence” is the presentation as the five senses in one’s own and others’ streams; “seeming of self” is the afflicted mind, owing to conjunction with self-delusion and the like; “seeming of cognition” is the six cognitions. “And the cognition does not have that object,” for the “object/existence/self/cognition”-seeming lacks true form, and the seeming of self and cognition is false-seeming,

children.text:
abhūtaparikalpatvaṃ siddham asya bhavaty ataḥ /
na tathā sarvathābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for this, the status of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> is established; yet not so as absolute non-existence,

body.text: yasmān na tathāsya bhāvo yathā pratibhāsa utpadyate / na ca sarvathābhāvo bhrāntimātrasyotpādāt/ kimarthaṃ punas tasyābhāva eva neṣyate / yasmāt /
body.translated_text: Because its being is not as it appears when it arises, nor is there absolute non-existence, since mere error does arise; why then is sheer non-existence of it not to be asserted? Because

children.translated_text: Liberation is taught as from its cessation, I.4

body.text: anyathā na bandho na mokṣaḥ prasidhyed iti saṃkleśavyavadānāpavādadoṣaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: Otherwise, neither bondage nor liberation would be established—there would be the fault of denying both defilement and purification,
c. Collecting-characteristic

body.text: evam abhūtaparikalpasya svalakṣaṇaṃ khyāpayitvā saṃgrahalakṣaṇaṃ khyāpayati / abhūtaparikalpamātre sati yathā trayāṇāṃ svabhāvānāṃ saṃgraho bhavati /
body.translated_text: Having thus made known the own-characteristic of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, he makes known the collecting-characteristic—how, when there is mere <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, the collection of the three natures is obtained,

children.text:
kalpitaḥ paratantraś ca pariniṣpanna eva ca /
arthād abhūtakalpāc ca dvayābhāvāc ca deśitaḥ // I.5
children.translated_text: The imagined, the dependent, and indeed the perfectly accomplished are taught from the standpoint of the meaning, from <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (imaginary construction), and from the absence of duality, I.5

body.text: arthaḥ parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ / abhūtaparikalpaḥ paratantraḥ svabhāvaḥ / grāhyagrāhakābhāvaḥ pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: The “meaning” is the <s>parikalpita</s> (imagined) own-nature; <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> is the <s>paratantra</s> (dependent) own-nature; the absence of grasper and grasped is the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfectly accomplished) own-nature,
d. Mark of the means of entry into the non-real characteristic
Now, with respect to that very <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, he elucidates the mark of the means for entering the non-real characteristic,
Mvbh 20

children.text:
upalabdhiṃ samāśritya nopalabdhiḥ prajāyate /
nopalabdhiṃ samāśritya nopalabdhiḥ prajāyate // I.6
children.translated_text: Relying upon apprehension, non-apprehension arises; relying upon non-apprehension, non-apprehension arises, I.6

body.text: vijñaptimātropalabdhiṃ niśrityārthānupalabdhir jāyate / arthānupalabdhiṃ niśritya vijñaptimātrasyāpy anupalabdhir jāyate / evam asallakṣaṇaṃ grāhyagrāhakayoḥ praviśati /
body.translated_text: Relying upon apprehension as mere <s>vijñapti</s> (representation), non-apprehension of objects arises; relying upon non-apprehension of objects, even non-apprehension of mere <s>vijñapti</s> arises; in this way the non-real characteristic enters into grasper and grasped,
From apprehension, then, the nature of non-apprehension is established,
Because, in the absence of an object to be apprehended, apprehension is inapplicable,

children.text: tasmāc ca samatā jñeyā nopalambhopalambhayoḥ // I.7
children.translated_text: And from this, the equality of non-apprehension and apprehension is to be understood, I.7

body.text: upalabdher upalabdhitvenāsiddhatvād abhūtārthapratibhāsatayā tūpalabdhir ity ucyate 'nupalabdhisvabhāvāpi satī
body.translated_text: Because apprehension, as apprehension, is not established, yet apprehension is said to be of the nature of non-apprehension, inasmuch as it appears as an unreal object,
e. Mark of division
Now he makes known the mark of division of that very <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>,
And <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> is mind and mental factors, within the three realms,
By the division into the <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Rūpa</s>, and <s>Ārūpya</s> spheres,
f. Mark by synonym
And he makes known the mark by synonym,

children.text: tatrārthadṛṣṭir vijñānaṃ tadviśeṣe tu caitasāḥ // I.8
children.translated_text: Therein, the cognition is the seeing of the mere object, while, with respect to the specification of that, the mental factors, I.8

body.text: tatrārthamātre dṛṣṭir vijñānaṃ / arthaviśeṣe dṛṣṭiś caitasā vedanādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the seeing with regard to the mere object is cognition; the seeing with regard to the specified object is the mental factors—feeling and the rest,
g. Mark of functioning
And he makes known the mark of functioning,
Mvbh 21

children.text:
ekaṃ pratyayavijñānaṃ dvitīyam aupabhogikaṃ /
upabhogaparicchedaprerakās tatra caitasāḥ // I.9
children.translated_text: One is the condition-cognition; the second is for enjoyment; and there, the mental factors impel delimitation and enjoyment, I.9

body.text: ālayavijñānam anyeṣāṃ vijñānānāṃ pratyayatvāt pratyayavijñānaṃ / tatpratyayaṃ pravṛttivijñānam aupabhogikaṃ / upabhogo vedanā / paricchedaḥ saṃjñā / prerakāḥ saṃskārā vijñānasya cetanāmanaskārādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse-cognition), being the condition of the other cognitions, is the condition-cognition; the cognition that has that as its condition is the functioning cognition, for enjoyment; enjoyment is feeling; delimitation is conception; the impellers are formations—intention, attention, and the like of cognition,
h. Mark of affliction
And he makes known the mark of affliction,

children.text:
chādanād ropaṇāc caiva nayanāt saṃparigrahāt /
pūraṇāt triparicchedād upabhogāc ca karṣaṇāt // I.10
children.translated_text: By covering and by planting, and by leading and by appropriation, by filling, by triple delimitation, by enjoyment, and by dragging, I.10

body.translated_text: By binding and by directing-toward, and by suffering, the world is afflicted,

body.text: tatra cchādanād avidyayā yathābhūtadarśanavibandhanāt / ropaṇāt saṃskārair vijñāne karmavāsanāyāḥ pratiṣṭhāpanāt / nayanād vijñānenopapattisthānasaṃprāpaṇāt / saṃparigrahān nāmarūpeṇātmabhāvasya / pūraṇāt ṣaḍāyatanena / triparicchedāt sparśena / upabhogād vedanayā / karṣaṇāt tṛṣṇayā karmākṣiptasya punarbhavasya [/] nibandhanād upādānair vijñānasyotpattyanukūleṣu kāmādiṣu / ābhimukhyād bhavena kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ punarbhave vipākadānāyābhimukhīkaraṇāt / duḥkhanāj jātyā jarāmaraṇena ca parikliśyate jagat / so 'yaṃ /
body.translated_text: Therein, by covering is meant the fettering of seeing-as-it-is by ignorance; by planting, the establishing of the karmic latencies of action in cognition through formations; by leading, the bringing of a being by cognition to the place of re-arising; by appropriation, the embodied complex through name-and-form; by filling, by the six sense-bases; by triple delimitation, by contact; by enjoyment, by feeling; by dragging, by craving, of the future existence propelled by action; by binding, by the appropriations, whereby cognition is bound to objects such as desire that are conducive to its arising; by directing-toward, the orienting of action done in existence (<s>bhava</s>) toward giving its maturation in a future existence; by suffering, the world is tormented by birth and by aging-and-death; thus this

children.text: tredhā dvedhā ca saṃkleśaḥ saptadhābhūtakalpanāt // I.11
children.translated_text: Affliction is threefold and twofold, on account of imaginary construction it is sevenfold, I.11

body.text: tredhā saṃkleśaḥ / kleśasaṃkleśaḥ karmasaṃkleśaḥ janmasaṃkleśaś ca / tatra kleśasaṃkleśo 'vidyātṛṣṇopādānāni / karmasaṃkleśaḥ saṃskārā bhavaś ca / janmasaṃkleśaḥ śeṣāṇy aṅgāni / dvedhā saṃkleśaḥ / hetusaṃkleśaḥ phalasaṃkleśaś ca /

children.translated_text: Mvbh 22

children.text: tatra hetusaṃkleśaḥ kleśakarmasvabhāvair aṅgaiḥ phalasaṃkleśaś ca śeṣaiḥ / saptadhā saṃkleśaḥ saptavidho hetuḥ / viparyāsahetuḥ / ākṣepahetuḥ i upanayahetuḥ / parigrahahetuḥ / upabhogahetuḥ / ākarṣaṇahetuḥ / udvegahetuś ca / tatra viparyāsahetur avidyā / ākṣepahetuḥ saṃskārāḥ / upanayahetur vijñānaṃ / parigrahahetur nāmarūpaṣaḍāyatane / upabhogahetuḥ sparśavedane / ākarṣaṇahetus tṛṣṇopādānabhavāḥ / udvegahetur jātijarāmaraṇe / sarvaś caiṣa saṃkleśo 'bhūtaparikalpāt pravartata iti /
children.translated_text: Therein, affliction as cause, with the limbs whose nature is defilements and actions; and affliction as result, with the remaining [limbs]; affliction is sevenfold; the cause is sevenfold: the cause as inversion (<s>viparyāsahetu</s>); the cause as impelling (<s>ākṣepahetu</s>); the cause as bringing-in (<s>upanayahetu</s>); the cause as appropriation (<s>parigrahahetu</s>); the cause as enjoyment (<s>upabhogahetu</s>); the cause as drawing-in (<s>ākarṣaṇahetu</s>); and the cause as agitation (<s>udvegahetu</s>); therein, the cause as inversion is ignorance; the cause as impelling is formations; the cause as bringing-in is cognition; the cause as appropriation is name-and-form and the six sense-bases; the cause as enjoyment is contact and feeling; the cause as drawing-in is craving, appropriation, and existence (<s>bhava</s>); the cause as agitation is birth, aging, and death; and all this affliction proceeds from <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (imaginary construction),

body.translated_text: Affliction is threefold: affliction as defilements; affliction as actions; and affliction as birth. Therein, affliction as defilements is ignorance, craving, and appropriation; affliction as actions is formations and existence (<s>bhava</s>); affliction as birth is the remaining factors. Affliction is twofold: affliction as cause and affliction as result,
Summary meaning of <s>Abhūtaparikalpa</s>

body.text: piṇḍārthaḥ punar abhūtaparikalpasya navavidhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitaṃ bhavati / sallakṣaṇaṃ / asallakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ / saṃgrahalakṣaṇaṃ [/] asallakṣaṇānupraveśopāyalakṣaṇaṃ / prabhedalakṣaṇaṃ / paryāyalakṣaṇaṃ / pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ / saṃkleśalakṣaṇañ ca /
body.translated_text: As for the summary meaning, the ninefold characteristic of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> is made clear: the mark of the existent; the mark of the non-existent; the own-characteristic; the collecting-characteristic; the mark of the means of entry into the non-real characteristic; the mark of division; the mark by synonym; the mark of functioning; and the mark of affliction,
2. <s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)

body.text: evam abhūtaparikalpaṃ khyāpayitvā yathā śūnyatā vijñeyā tan nirdiśati /
body.translated_text: Having thus made known <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, he indicates how <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is to be understood,

children.text:
lakṣaṇaṃ cātha paryāyas tadartho bheda eva ca /
sādhanaṃ ceti vijñeyaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ samāsataḥ // I.12
children.translated_text: The characteristic, and then the synonyms; its meaning; and the division as well; and the means [of realization]—such, in brief, is to be understood for <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), I.12

body.translated_text: a. The characteristic of <s>Śūnyatā</s>
How is the characteristic to be understood?

body.text: dvayābhāvo hy abhāvasya bhāvaḥ śūnyasya lakṣaṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: The absence of duality, indeed the existence of absence—this is the characteristic of the empty,

children.translated_text: Mvbh 23

children.text: lakṣaṇam ity abhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇatvaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ paridīpitaṃ bhavati / yaś cāsau tadabhāvasvabhāvaḥ sa /
children.translated_text: —is the characteristic; thus the being-a-mark of an absence-nature is made clear for <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness); and that very absence-nature is such that

body.translated_text: The absence of duality—of grasper and grasped; and the existence of that absence, as emptiness,
It is not existence, nor indeed non-existence,

body.text: kathaṃ na bhāvo yasmāt dvayasyābhāvaḥ / kathaṃ nābhāvo yasmāt dvayābhāvasya bhāvaḥ / etac ca śūnyatāyā lakṣaṇaṃ / tasmād abhūtaparikalpān
body.translated_text: How is it not existence? Because it is the absence of duality; how is it not non-existence? Because it is the existence of the absence of duality; and this is the characteristic of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness); therefore, of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (imaginary construction),

children.translated_text: there is neither the characteristic of difference nor of identity, I.13

body.text: pṛthaktve sati dharmād anyā dharmateti na yujyate / anityatāduḥkhatāvat / ekatve sati viśuddhyālambanaṃ jñānaṃ na syāt sāmānyalakṣaṇañ ca / etena tattvānyatvavinirmuktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: If there were difference, it would not be fitting to say, “Dharma is other than <s>dharma</s>” (the quality is other than the qualified); as with impermanence and suffering; if there were identity, the knowledge whose object is purification would not exist, nor the general characteristic; by this, a characteristic free from “is” and “is-other” is made clear,
b. The synonyms of <s>Śūnyatā</s>
How are the synonyms to be understood?

children.text:
tathatā bhūtakoṭiś cānimittaṃ paramārthatā /
dharmadhātuś ca paryāyāḥ śūnyatāyāḥ samāsataḥ // I.14
children.translated_text: <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), and the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), and the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>), and the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthatā</s>), and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) are, in brief, synonyms of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), I.14

body.translated_text: c. The meaning of the synonyms of <s>Śūnyatā</s>
How is the meaning of the synonyms to be understood?

children.text:
ananyathāviparyāsatannirodhāryagocaraiḥ /
hetutvāc cāryadharmāṇāṃ paryāyārtho yathākramaṃ // I.15
children.translated_text: By the meanings of “not otherwise,” “free from inversion,” “cessation of signs,” “the Arya-domain,” and because of being the cause of the noble qualities—such, in order, is the meaning of the synonyms, I.15

body.text: ananyathārthena tathātā nityan tathaiveti kṛtvā [/] aviparyāsārthena bhūtakoṭiḥ viparyāsāvastutvāt / nimittanirodhārthenānimittaṃ sarvanimittābhāvāt / āryajñānagocaratvāt paramārthaḥ / paramajñānaviṣayatvād [/] āryadharmahetutvād dharmadhātuḥ /

children.translated_text: Mvbh 24

children.text: āryadharmāṇān tadālambanaprabhavatvāt / hetvartho hy atra dhātvarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: —because the noble qualities arise having that as their object; here, the meaning of “cause” is the meaning of “source/element” (<s>dhātu</s>),

body.translated_text: By the meaning “not otherwise,” <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), since it is perpetual as just thus; by the meaning “free from inversion,” the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), because inversions are unreal; by the meaning of cessation of signs, the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>), because of the absence of all signs; because it is the domain of noble knowledge, the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>), since it is the object of supreme knowledge; and because it is the cause of noble qualities, the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
d. The divisions of <s>Śūnyatā</s>
How is the division of <s>śūnyatā</s> to be known?
It is defiled, and it is pure,

body.text: ity asyāḥ prabhedaḥ / kasyām avasthāyāṃ saṃkliṣṭā kasyāṃ viśuddhā /
body.translated_text: —such is its division; in which condition is it defiled, and in which pure?
It is with stains, and without stains,

body.text: yadā saha malena vartate tadā saṃkliṣṭā / yadā prahīṇamalā tadā viśuddhā / yadi samalā bhūtvā nirmalā bhavati kathaṃ vikāradharmiṇītvād anityā na bhavati / yasmād asyāḥ
body.translated_text: When it operates together with stain, then it is defiled; when the stains are abandoned, then it is pure; if, being with stains, it becomes without stains, how is it that, as a bearer of alteration, it does not become impermanent? Because for it

children.translated_text: purity is accepted like the clarity of water, of gold, and of space, I.1

body.text: āgantukamalāpagamān na tu tasyāḥ svabhāvānyatvaṃ bhavati /

The sixteenfold <s>śūnyatā</s>

body.text: ayam aparaḥ prabhedaḥ ṣoḍaśavidhā śūnyatā / adhyātmaśūnyatā / bahirdhāśūnyatā / adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā / mahāśūnyatā / śūnyatāśūnyatā / paramārthaśūnyatā / saṃskṛtaśūnyatā / asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā / atyantaśūnyatā / anavarāgrasūnyatā / anavakāraśūnyatā / prakṛtiśūnyatā / lakṣaṇaśūnyatā / sarvadharmaśūnyatā / abhāvaśūnyatā / abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā ca / saiṣā samāsato veditavyā /
body.translated_text: This is another division: the sixteenfold <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)—<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal-emptiness), <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external-emptiness), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-and-external-emptiness), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great-emptiness), <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness-of-emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness as ultimate), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the unconditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (utter-emptiness), <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (beginning-and-endless-emptiness), <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s> (non-diminishing-emptiness), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of nature), <s>lakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of characteristics), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all phenomena), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), and <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature-of-non-existence); this, in summary, is to be understood,

children.text:
bhoktṛbhojanataddehapratiṣṭhāvastuśūnyatā /

children.translated_text: Emptiness of enjoyer, of what is enjoyed, and of the support-body of those; and that which, however, is seen—by whom, how, and for what purpose—of that there is emptiness, I.17

body.text: tatra bhoktṛśūnyatā (/) ādhyātmikāny āyatanāny ārabdhā bhojanaśūnyatā bāhyāni / taddehas tayor bhoktṛbhojanayor yad adhiṣṭhānaṃ śarīraṃ [/] tasya śūnyatādhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatety ucyate / pratiṣṭhāvastu bhājanalokaḥ [/] tasya vistīrṇatvāc chūnyatā mahāśūnyatety ucyate / tac cādhyātmikāyatanādi yena śūnyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śūnyatājñānena [/] tasya śūnyatā śūnyatāśūnyatā / yathā ca dṛṣṭaṃ paramārthākāreṇa tasya śūnyatā paramārtha śūnyatā / yadarthaṃ ca bodhisatvaḥ prapadyate tasya ca śūnyatā / kimarthañ ca prapadyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, emptiness of the enjoyer is the internal sense-bases; emptiness of what is enjoyed is the external ones; the body of those two—the enjoyer and what is enjoyed—the basis, the body, of that there is emptiness, and this is called internal-and-external-emptiness; the supporting-thing is the receptacle-world; because of its vastness, its emptiness is called great-emptiness; and that internal sense-bases and the like, by which it is seen as empty—by knowledge of emptiness—of that there is emptiness, [namely] emptiness-of-emptiness; and as it is seen in the mode of the ultimate, of that there is emptiness, [namely] emptiness as ultimate; and for the sake of which the <s>bodhisattva</s> undertakes [it], of that too there is emptiness; and for what purpose does he undertake [it]?
For the attainment of the twofold auspicious,
Of the wholesome conditioned and unconditioned,
And always for the welfare of beings,
For the sake of the utmost welfare of beings,
And for the purpose of abandoning <s>saṃsāra</s>,

body.text: anavarāgrasya hi saṃsārasya śūnyatām apaśyan khinnaḥ saṃsāraṃ parityajeta /
body.translated_text: For, not seeing the emptiness of beginning-and-endless <s>saṃsāra</s>, one would grow weary and abandon <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.translated_text: And for the inexhaustibility of the wholesome, I.18

body.text: nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇe 'pi yan nāvakirati notsṛjati tasya śūnyatā (/)

children.translated_text: Mvbh 26
and this is called non-diminishing-emptiness,

body.translated_text: And even in <s>nirvāṇa</s> with no residue of substratum, that which neither scatters nor discards—of that there is emptiness,
And for the purification of the lineage (<s>gotra</s>),
For lineage indeed is nature, since it is intrinsic,
For the acquisition of marks and secondary signs,
For the attainment of the marks of a Great Person together with the secondary signs,

children.translated_text: For the purification of the Buddha-qualities does the <s>bodhisattva</s> undertake [it], I.19

body.text: balavaiśāradyāveṇikādīnāṃ / evan tāvac caturdaśānāṃ śūnyatānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyaṃ / kā punar atra śūnyatā /
body.translated_text: Such are, thus far, the established accounts of fourteen emptinesses; what, then, here is emptiness?

children.text:
pudgalasyātha dharmāṇām abhāvaḥ śūnyatātra hi /
tadabhāvasya sadbhāvas tasmin sā śūnyatāparā // I.20
children.translated_text: Emptiness here is the non-existence of the person or of phenomena; and the existence of that non-existence—therein, that is the other emptiness, I.20

body.text: pudgaladharmābhāvaś ca śūnyatā / tadabhāvasya ca sadbhāvaḥ [/] tasmin yathokte bhoktrādau sānyā śūnyateti [/] śūnyatālakṣaṇakhyāpanārthaṃ dvividhām ante śūnyatāṃ vyavasthāpayati / abhāvaśūnyatām abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāṃ ca / pudgaladharmasamāropasya tacchūnyatāpavādasya ca parihārārthaṃ yathākramaṃ / evaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ prabhedo vijñeyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The non-existence of person and phenomena is emptiness; and the existence of that non-existence—therein, with respect to the aforesaid enjoyer and so on—this is another emptiness; in order to make known the characteristic of emptiness, he establishes, at the end, a twofold emptiness: emptiness of non-existence, and emptiness of the nature-of-non-existence, respectively, for the avoidance of the superimposition of person-and-phenomena and of the negation of that emptiness; thus the division of emptiness is to be understood,
e. The means of realizing <s>śūnyatā</s>
How is the means to be understood?

Because of the luminousness of mind,

Summary-meaning of <s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)

body.text: tatra śūnyatāyāḥ piṇḍārthaḥ / lakṣaṇato vyavasthānataś ca veditavyaḥ / tatra lakṣaṇato 'bhāvalakṣaṇato bhāvalakṣaṇataś ca / bhāvalakṣaṇaṃ punar bhāvābhāvavinirmuktalakṣaṇataś ca / tatvānyatvavinirmuktalakṣaṇataś ca / vyavasthānaṃ punaḥ paryāyādivyavasthānato veditavyaṃ / tatraitayā catuḥprakāradeśanayā śūnyatāyāḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ / karmalakṣaṇaṃ / saṃkleśavyavadānalakṣaṇaṃ / yuktilakṣaṇaṃ codbhāvitaṃ bhavati / vikalpatrāsakauśīdyavicikitsopaśāntaye /
body.translated_text: Therein, the summary-meaning of <s>śūnyatā</s> is to be understood by way of definition and by way of establishment; therein, by way of definition, by the characteristic of non-existence and by the characteristic of existence; and again, the “existence-characteristic” is by the characteristic of being free from existence-and-non-existence, and by the characteristic of being free from identity-and-otherness; again, establishment is to be understood by the establishment beginning with synonyms; here, by this fourfold manner of exposition, there are brought to light the own-characteristic of <s>śūnyatā</s>, the action-characteristic, the characteristic of affliction-and-purification, and the characteristic according to reasoning, for the pacification of conceptualization, fear, sloth, and doubt,
In the Madhyāntavibhāga, the delimitation of the non-instant (akṣaṇa) is first,
Mvbh 28
CHAPTER II. Delimitation of Obstructions
1. The five obstructions beginning with “pervasive”
Regarding obstruction, he says,

children.translated_text: The avoidance of what is pervasive, particular, excessive, equal, and of appropriation—twofold obstruction is declared,

body.text: tatra vyāpi kleśajñeyāvaraṇaṃ bodhisatvagotrakāṇāṃ kaṃ sākalyāt / prādeśikaṃ kleśāvaranaṃ śrāvakādigotrakāṇāṃ / udriktaṃ teṣām eva rāgādicaritānāṃ / samaṃ samabhāgacaritānāṃ / saṃsārādānatyāgāvaraṇaṃ bodhisatvagotrakāṇām apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇāvaraṇād ity etad yathāyogam ubhayeṣām āvaraṇam ākhyātaṃ / bodhisatvagotrakānāṃ śrāvakādigotrakāṇāṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the pervasive obstruction of afflictions and knowables is, in its entirety, for those of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-lineage; the particular obstruction of afflictions is for those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> and the like lineages; the excessive is for those very ones who are of the character of lust and so on; the equal is for those of equal-share character; the obstruction of appropriation-and-abandonment with respect to <s>saṃsāra</s> is for those of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-lineage, because of the obstruction of non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>; thus, as is fitting, this twofold obstruction is declared for both—for those of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-lineage and for those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> and the like lineages,
2. The obstruction of the nine fetters in the path of practice
Further,

children.translated_text: Ninefold is the characteristic of affliction, II.1

body.translated_text: The fetters are the obstruction,
The nine fetters are the obstruction of afflictions; of whom is this obstruction?

children.translated_text: Of agitation and of equanimity, and of non-seeing of reality,
Mvbh 29

children.text: upekṣīyāḥ / tena hi pratikūlam api pratighavastu upekṣituṃ na śaknoti / śeṣāni tattvadarśanasyāvaraṇaṃ / kathaṃ kṛtvā / tāni hi yathākramaṃ /
children.translated_text: of the equanimous; for by that, he is not able to regard with equanimity even an adverse object of aversion; the remaining are the obstruction of the seeing of reality; how so?—those, in order,

body.translated_text: The fetter of indulgence is the obstruction of the zealous; the fetter of aversion is

children.translated_text: With respect to the view of a real person, and of that very object; and with respect to the jewels of cessation and path, and indeed esteem for gains and honors; in the understanding of ascetic refinement, II.2

children.text:
nirodhamārgaratneṣu lābhasatkāra eva ca /
saṃlekhasya parijñāne /
children.translated_text: The fetters become an obstruction; for the fetter of conceit, in the discerning of the view of a real person, becomes an obstruction, because at the time of realization, by the force of the inner and intermediary uprisings of the conceit “I am,” that is not abandoned; the fetter of ignorance, in the discerning of the object of the view of a real person, because of the non-discernment of the aggregates of appropriation; the fetter of views, in the discerning of the truth of cessation, because of intimidation by the extremes of eternalism with respect to the person and of annihilationism—thereby—its disparagement by wrong view; the fetter of grasping (parāmarśa), in the discerning of the truth of the path, because of grasping at purification of what is otherwise (than the path); the fetter of doubt, in the discerning of the Three Jewels, because of lack of faith in their qualities; the fetter of envy, in the discerning of gains and honors, because of not seeing their faults; the fetter of stinginess, in the discerning of ascetic refinement, because of fixation on embellishment,

body.text: saṃyojanāny āvaraṇaṃ bhavaṃti / mānasaṃyojanaṃ hi satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñāne bhavaty āvaraṇaṃ / abhisamayakāle sāntaravyantarāsmimānasamudācāravaśena tadaprahāṇāt / avidyāsaṃyojanaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭivastuparijñāne / tenopādānaskandhāparijñānāt / dṛṣṭisaṃyojanaṃ nirodhasatyaparijñāne / satkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭibhyāṃ taduttrāsāt [/] mithyādṛṣṭyā cāpavādāt / parāmarśasaṃyojanaṃ mārgasatyaparijñāne / anyathāgraśuddhiparāmarṣaṇāt / vicikitsāsaṃyojanaṃ ratnatrayaparijñāne tadguṇānabhiśraddhānāt / īrṣyāsaṃyojanaṃ lābhasatkāraparijñāne taddoṣādarśanāt / mātsaryasaṃyojanaṃ saṃlekhaparijñāne pariṣkārādhyavasānāt /
body.translated_text: The fetters become the covering. The fetter of conceit is the covering in the understanding of the view of the body, due to the persistence of the inner and outer self-conceit at the time of realization, due to not abandoning it. The fetter of ignorance is the covering in the understanding of the object of the view of the body, due to not understanding the aggregates of clinging. The fetter of view is the covering in the understanding of the truth of cessation, due to fear from the views of the body and eternal grasping, and due to criticism by wrong view. The fetter of attachment is the covering in the understanding of the truth of the path, due to attachment to purity of grasping otherwise. The fetter of doubt is the covering in the understanding of the three jewels, due to lack of faith in their virtues. The fetter of jealousy is the covering in the understanding of gain and honor, due to the perception of their faults. The fetter of stinginess is the covering in the understanding of simplicity, due to the resolution in purification.
3. The <s>bodhisattva</s>-obstruction
a. The obstruction with respect to the ten virtues and the like

children.translated_text: Further, with respect to the wholesome and the like, it is tenfold, II.3

body.text: aparaṃ punar āvaraṇaṃ / daśavidhe śubhādau veditavyaṃ / kin tad āvaraṇaṃ ke ca śubhādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Further, another obstruction is to be known, in the tenfold wholesome and the like; what is that obstruction, and what are the wholesome and the like?

children.translated_text: Non-application; in a wrong sphere; what is effected by improper yoga; non-arising; non-attention; non-fulfillment of the accumulation, II.4
Desolation of lineage and of spiritual friend; weariness of mind,
The absence of lineage friends, the weariness of the mind,

body.translated_text: Mvbh 30

children.translated_text: And desolation of practice; dwelling among wicked people, II.5
Harshness; residual taints; from the three, unripe wisdom,

children.text: prakṛtyā caiva dauṣṭhulyaṃ kauśīdyaṃ ca pramāditā // II.6
children.translated_text: And harshness indeed by nature; sloth; heedlessness, II.6

children.text: saktir bhave ca bhoge ca līnacittatvam eva ca /

Lack of faith; premature certitude; and investigation merely according to what is heard, II.7

saddharme 'gauravaṃ lābhe gurutā kṛpatā tathā /
śrutavyasanam alpatvaṃ samādhyaparikarmitā // II.8
children.translated_text: Disrespect for the true Dharma; heaviness with respect to alms; and miserliness as well; addiction to hearing; littleness (meanness); and ill-preparation for concentration, II.8

body.translated_text: This is the obstruction; who are the wholesome and the like?

children.text:
śubhaṃ bodhiḥ samādānan dhīmattvābhrāntyanāvṛtī /
natyatrāso 'matsaritvaṃ vaśitvaṃ ca śubhādayaḥ // II.9
children.translated_text: The wholesome: awakening; undertaking; intelligence; non-delusion; unobstructedness; absence of haughtiness; fearlessness here; absence of envy; and mastery—these are the wholesome and the like, II.9

body.text: eṣāṃ śubhādīnāṃ kasya katy āvaraṇāni jñeyānīty āha /
body.translated_text: Regarding these wholesome and the like, he says: of which, how many obstructions are to be known?

body.text: trīṇi trīṇi ca eteṣāṃ jñeyāny āvaraṇāni hi /
body.translated_text: And indeed, for these, three, three obstructions are to be known,

body.text: kuśalasya trīṇy āvaraṇāni / aprayogo 'nāyatanaprayogo 'yoniśaḥprayogaś ca / bodhes trīṇi kuśalasyānutpattir amanasikaraṇaṃ / aparipūrṇasaṃbhāratā ca / samādānaṃ bodhicittotpādaḥ / tasya trīṇi gotravaidhuryaṃ kalyāṇamitravaidhuryaṃ / parikhedacittatā ca / dhīmatvaṃ bodhisatvatā / tasyāḥ prajñāne trīṇy āvaraṇāni pratipattivaidhuryaṃ kujanavāsaḥ / duṣṭajanavāsaś ca / tatra kujano mūrkhajanaḥ [/] duṣṭajanaḥ pratihataḥ / abhrāntes trīṇi viparyāsadauṣṭhulyaṃ / kleśādyāvaraṇatrayād anyatamāvaśiṣṭatā / vimuktiparipācinyāḥ (/) prajñāyā aparipakvatā ca / āvaraṇaprahāṇam anāvaraṇaṃ / tasya trīṇi sahajaṃ dauṣṭhulyaṃ / kauśīdyaṃ pramādaś ca / pariṇates trīṇi yair anyatra cittaṃ pariṇāmayati / nānuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau [/]
body.translated_text: For the wholesome, there are three obstructions: non-application; application in a wrong sphere; and application contrary to method (<s>ayonisaḥ-prayoga</s>) For awakening, three: non-arising of the wholesome; non-attention; and non-fulfillment of the accumulation; undertaking is the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> For this, three: desolation of lineage (<s>gotra-vaidhurya</s>); desolation of spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇa-mitra-vaidhurya</s>); and weariness-of-mind For intelligence, [namely] <s>bodhisattva</s>-hood; for its knowledge, three obstructions: desolation of practice (<s>pratipatti-vaidhurya</s>); dwelling among base people; and dwelling among wicked people; therein, a “base person” is a foolish person, [and] a “wicked person” is one obstructive For the unconfused, three: coarseness arising from inversion; the condition of something-or-other remaining from the triad of obstructions beginning with afflictions; and immaturity of the knowledge that ripens liberation; the abandoning of obstruction is non-obstruction; for this, three: innate coarseness; sloth; and heedlessness; for the deflected, three, by which he turns the mind elsewhere, not toward unsurpassed perfect awakening,
Mvbh 31

body.text: bhavasaktir bhogasaktir līnacittatā ca / atrāsasya trīṇi [/] asaṃbhāvanā pudgale / anadhimuktir dharme / yathārutavicāraṇārthe / amātsaryasya trīṇi saddharme 'gauravaṃ / lābhasatkārapūjāyāṃ gauravaṃ satveṣv akāruṇyaṃ ca / vaśitvasya trīṇi yair vibhutvaṃ na labhate [/] śrutavyasanaṃ dharmavyasanasaṃvartanīyakarmaprabhavanāt / alpaśrutatvaṃ / samādher aparikarmitatvaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Attachment to becoming; attachment to enjoyments; and mental torpor; for fearlessness here, three: non-conceivability regarding the person; non-resolution regarding the Dharma; and investigation merely according to what is heard, as to the matter of words For non-miserliness, three: disrespect for the true Dharma; regard for gains, honors, and worship; and lack of compassion toward beings For mastery, three, by which he does not obtain supremacy: addiction to hearing—arising from actions that conduce to addiction to Dharma-hearing; scant learning; and ill-preparation for concentration,
b. The ten causes

body.translated_text: Now, again, this obstruction—beginning with the wholesome—is to be understood, with respect to the relevant object, by means of the ten causes wherever there are ten causes; the ten causes are: the cause of arising, such as the eye and the like for eye-consciousness; the cause of abiding, such as the four nourishments for living beings; the cause of support, namely, whatever is the base for something, as, for example, the vessel-world for the world of beings; the cause of manifestation, such as light for visible form; the cause of alteration, such as fire and the like for cooking and the like; the cause of separation, such as a knife and the like for what is to be cut and the like; the cause of transformation, such as goldsmiths and the like for gold and so on in the state of bracelet and the like; the cause of co-conditioning (<s>saṃpratyaya</s>), such as smoke and the like for fire and the like; the cause of making-to-apprehend (<s>saṃpratyāyana</s>), such as a reason (<s>hetu</s>) for a thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>); the cause of attainment, such as the paths and the like for <s>nirvāṇa</s> and so on,

body.translated_text: For one who wishes to attain <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), from the very beginning, a root of the wholesome is to be generated; then, by the strengthening through the power of the root of the wholesome, <s>Bodhi</s> is to be attained; again, for the generation of that very root of the wholesome, there is the establishment of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the thought of awakening); the <s>bodhisattva</s> is the basis (support) of that <s>bodhicitta</s>; therefore, by that <s>bodhisattva</s> who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s> and obtained strengthening by the power of the root of the wholesome, having abandoned inversion (error), non-inversion (correct cognition) is to be generated; thereafter, with non-inversion on the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) all obstructions are to be abandoned; with obstructions abandoned, all roots of the wholesome are to be dedicated toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>); then, by the strengthening of dedication, one should not tremble in profound and exalted teachings of the Dharma; and with mind thus unshaken, seeing the qualities in the Dharmas, those Dharmas are to be thoroughly illuminated to others in detail; then that <s>bodhisattva</s>, thus endowed by the power of diverse qualities, swiftly

As to the bodhipakṣas,

children.translated_text: In the establishments of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), maladroitness with respect to the object is an obstruction; in right abandonings (<s>samyak-prahāṇa</s>), sloth; in the bases of supernormal potency (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the deficiency of concentration in both aspects; and in their fulfillment, from the lack of any one among zeal, vigor, mind, and inquiry; and in cultivation, from the deficiency of the formations of abandoning; in the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the non-imposition (failure to apply) of those that partake of liberation; in the powers (<s>bala</s>), the weakness of those very faculties, because of scattering by the opponents; in the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the fault of view, because they are empowered by the path of seeing; in the path-factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>), the fault of coarseness, because they are empowered by the path of cultivation,

Here, for the ten pāramitās, whatever fruit belongs to whatever pāramitā, that obstruction—by obstructing that (fruit)—becomes manifest as its obstruction; therein, for the perfection of giving (<s>dāna-pāramitā</s>), obstruction is obstruction to sovereignty and lordship; for the perfection of morality (<s>śīla-pāramitā</s>), obstruction to a good destination; for the perfection of patience (<s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s>), obstruction to non-abandonment of beings; for the perfection of vigor (<s>vīrya-pāramitā</s>), obstruction in the diminishing of faults and the increase of qualities; for the perfection of concentration (<s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s>), obstruction to bringing trainees to maturation; for the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñā-pāramitā</s>), obstruction to liberation; for the perfection of skill in means (<s>upāya-kauśalya-pāramitā</s>), obstruction to the inexhaustibility of giving and so forth; for dedication to awakening (<s>bodhi-pariṇāmanā</s>), because of making that inexhaustible; for the perfection of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna-pāramitā</s>), obstruction to the continuous engagement of the wholesome in every birth—because, by the power of aspiration, there is the inclusion of a rebirth conducive to that; for the perfection of power (<s>bala-pāramitā</s>), obstruction to making that very wholesome fixed (irreversible), because, without the strengths of discriminative analysis and cultivation (<s>pratisaṃkhyāna-bhāvanā-bala</s>), the adversaries are not overcome; for the perfection of knowledge (<s>jñāna-pāramitā</s>), obstruction to the enjoyment and ripening of Dharma for oneself and others, because of a failure to understand the meaning of what is heard as it truly is,

children.translated_text: The fourfold mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>): mastery of non-conceptuality, mastery of purity of fields, mastery of knowledge, and mastery of action; therein, the basis for the first two masteries is in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and it is precisely by the eighth bhūmi that it is penetrated; the basis for mastery of knowledge is on the ninth, through the attainment of discriminative knowledge (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>); the basis for mastery of action is on the tenth, through accomplishing the welfare of beings by creations (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) according to wish,

body.translated_text: For, by the first bhūmi indeed, he penetrates the meaning of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of Dharma) as all-pervading, by which he attains equality of self and other; by the second, the meaning of what is foremost, by which it is thus for him: “Therefore, then, for us, in equal derivation (emanation), the yoga to be done is precisely the derivation that fully purifies all aspects”; by the third, the meaning of the foremost in outflow (derivation), by which, having understood the supremacy of the heard diffusion (emanation) of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, for the sake of that he would cast himself even into a pit of fire measuring a three-thousand great-thousand world-system; by the fourth, the meaning of non-appropriation, for thus even thirst for Dharma (<s>dharmatṛṣṇā</s>) is turned back; by the fifth, the meaning of non-diversity of continuum, by means of ten equalities of the purification of mind and intention; by the sixth, the meaning of stainless purity, through the direct realization in dependent arising (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) that “there is no Dharma whatsoever that is defiled or purified”; by the seventh, the meaning of non-plurality, through signlessness, from the non-occurrence of plurality of signs of Dharma such as sūtra and so on; by the eighth, the meaning of non-loss and non-gain, from the attainment of the patience with the non-arising of Dharmas (<s>anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti</s>), because one sees no loss or increase of any Dharma in defilement or in purification,

body.translated_text: The gist of the obstructions: the great obstruction is that which is pervasive; the thin obstruction is that which is localized; the obstruction of application is that which is excessive; the obstruction of attainment is that which is equal; the obstruction of distinctive attainment is that which lies in the absence of appropriation; the obstruction of right application is the ninefold obstruction of afflictions; the obstruction of cause is that which, beginning with the wholesome, pertains to the domain of the tenfold meanings of cause; the obstruction of entry into reality is that which is in the <s>bodhipakṣa</s>-factors; the obstruction of the unsurpassed wholesome is that which is in the <s>pāramitā</s>s; the obstruction of their distinctive course is that which is in the bhūmis; the obstruction of summary is that which, in summary, is twofold,
