children.translated_text: Unreal and permanent, and real yet not of the nature of reality, and both real-and-unreal in respect of reality—thus the three natures are maintained, III.3

body.text: parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ nityam asad ity etat parikalpitasvabhāve tatvam aviparītatvāt [/] paratantralakṣaṇaṃ sac ca na ca tatvato bhrāntatvād ity etat paratantrasvabhāve tatvaṃ / pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ sadasattatvataś cety etat (/) pariniṣpannasvabhāve tatvaṃ /
body.translated_text: “The characteristic of the imagined (parikalpita) is permanent and unreal”—this is reality (<s>tattva</s>) in the <s>parikalpita</s>-nature, because of non-inversion; “the characteristic of the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) is both real and not, not in respect of reality, because it is delusive”—this is reality in the <s>paratantra</s>-nature; “the characteristic of the perfectly accomplished (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) is both real-and-unreal with respect to reality”—this is reality in the <s>pariniṣpanna</s>-nature,
2. Mark-reality
What is mark-reality (<s>lakṣaṇatattva</s>),

children.translated_text: Here, the seeing of superimposition and refutation regarding dharmas and persons (<s>pudgala</s>),

children.text: grāhyagrāhakayoś cāpi bhāvābhāve ca darśanaṃ // III.4
children.translated_text: And also regarding the apprehended and the apprehender, and regarding existence and non-existence, III.4

children.text: yajjñānān na pravarteta tad dhi tatvasya lakṣaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: That by whose cognition one would not proceed—that indeed is the mark of reality,

body.text: pudgaladharmayoḥ samāropāpavādadarśanaṃ yasya jñānān na pravartate / tat parikalpitasvabhāve tatvalakṣaṇaṃ / grāhyagrāhakayoḥ samāropāpavādadarśanaṃ yasya jñānān na pravartate / tat paratantrasvabhāve tatvalakṣaṇaṃ / bhāvābhāvasamāropāpavādadarśanaṃ yasya jñānān na pravartate / tat pariniṣpannasvabhāve tatvalakṣaṇaṃ / etan mūlatatve lakṣaṇam aviparītaṃ lakṣaṇatatvam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: That, by whose cognition the seeing of superimposition and refutation with respect to persons and dharmas does not proceed—that is the mark of reality in the <s>parikalpita</s>-nature; that, by whose cognition the seeing of superimposition and refutation with respect to the apprehended and the apprehender does not proceed—that is the mark of reality in the <s>paratantra</s>-nature; that, by whose cognition the seeing of superimposition and refutation with respect to existence and non-existence does not proceed—that is the mark of reality in the <s>pariniṣpanna</s>-nature; this non-inverted mark, within root-reality, is what is called mark-reality,
3. Non-inversion-reality

body.text: aviparyāsatatvaṃ nityādiviparyāsapratipakṣeṇānityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmatā mūlatatve yathākramaṃ [/] kathaṃ ca tatrānityatāditā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Non-inversion-reality (<s>aviparyāsatattva</s>): as the counteragent to the inversions beginning with permanence, impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self are, in root-reality, to be known in order; and how, there, are impermanence and the rest to be understood,

children.translated_text: For the object of the unreal is the meaning of impermanence, characterized by arising and disintegration, III.5
In root-reality, in due order, by impurity and purity,

body.translated_text: Mvbh 39

body.text: trayo hi svabhāvā mūlatatvaṃ [/] teṣu yathākramam
body.translated_text: For the three natures are root-reality; among them, in due order,
The object of the unreal is the meaning of impermanence,
The meaning of arising-and-disintegration, and the meaning of impurity-and-purity,

children.translated_text: Suffering is said, in another respect, to be characterized as the mark of appropriation; and in respect of relation, III.6

body.text: mūlatatve yathākramaṃ duḥkham upādānataḥ pudgaladharmābhiniveśopādānāt / lakṣaṇatas triduḥkhatālakṣaṇatvāt / saṃbandhataś ca duḥkhasaṃbandhāt [/] tatraiva mūlatatve yathākramaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: In root-reality, in due order, suffering is from appropriation—because of the appropriation that is the fixation on person and dharmas; as to mark, because its mark is the threefold suffering; and as to relation, because of relation to suffering; this, there itself in root-reality, is to be understood in due order,

body.text: abhāvaś cāpy atadbhāvaḥ prakṛtiḥ śūnyatā matā /
body.translated_text: And non-existence is also other-natured non-existence; its nature is said to be emptiness,

body.text: parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ na kenacit prakāreṇāstīty abhāva evāsya śūnyatā paratantralakṣaṇaṃ tathā nāsti yathā parikalpyate na tu sarvathā nāstīti tasyātadbhāvaḥ (/) śūnyatā [/] pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ śūnyatāsvabhāvam eveti prakṛtir evāsya śūnyatā /
body.translated_text: For the characteristic of the <s>parikalpita</s> does not exist in any way whatever—therefore its emptiness is precisely non-existence; for the characteristic of the <s>paratantra</s> does not exist as it is imagined, though it does not absolutely not exist—therefore its emptiness is other-natured non-existence; for the characteristic of the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> is precisely of the nature of emptiness—therefore its nature itself is emptiness,

children.text: alakṣaṇaṃ ca nairātmyaṃ tadvilakṣaṇam eva ca // III.7
children.translated_text: And non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>) is non-mark, and it is precisely that which is distinct from that, III.7
And its own-mark is also stated,

body.text: parikalpitasya svabhāvasya lakṣaṇam eva nāstīty alakṣaṇam evāsya nairātmyaṃ [/] paratantrasyāsti lakṣaṇaṃ na tu yathā parikalpyata iti tadvilakṣaṇam asya lakṣaṇan nairātmyaṃ / pariniṣpannas tu svabhāvo nairātmyam eveti prakṛtir evāsya nairātmyam iti trividhe mūlatatve trividhānityatā paridīpitā asadarthānityatā utpādabhaṅgānityatā samalanirmalānityatā ca / trividhā duḥkhatā upādānaduḥkhatā lakṣaṇaduḥkhatā saṃbandhaduḥkhatā

children.translated_text: Mvbh 40

children.text: ca / trividhā śūnyatā abhāvaśūnyatā atadbhāvaśūnyatā svabhāvaśūnyatā ca trividhaṃ nairātmyaṃ alakṣaṇanairātmyaṃ / vilakṣaṇanairātmyaṃ svalakṣaṇanairātmyaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: And the threefold emptiness: emptiness as non-existence, emptiness as other-natured non-existence, and emptiness as self-nature-emptiness; and the threefold non-self: non-self as non-mark, non-self as distinct-from-the-mark, and non-self as own-mark-non-self,

body.translated_text: For the nature of the <s>parikalpita</s> has no mark at all—therefore its non-self is precisely non-mark; for the <s>paratantra</s> there is a mark, but not as it is imagined—therefore its non-self is the mark that is distinct from that; but the <s>pariniṣpanna</s>-nature is itself non-self—therefore its nature itself is non-self; thus, in the threefold root-reality, the threefold impermanence is made clear: the impermanence of the object that is unreal, the impermanence of arising-and-ceasing, and the impermanence of impurity-and-purity; the threefold suffering: suffering of appropriation, suffering as mark, and suffering as relation;
4. Fruit-and-cause-reality

body.text: phalahetumayan tatvaṃ tatraiva mūlatatve duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgasatyatvaṃ [/] kathaṃ trividhaṃ mūlatatvaṃ duḥkhādisatyatvaṃ [/] yatas tad anityādilakṣaṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: Fruit-and-cause reality (<s>phalahetumayatattva</s>): there itself, in root-reality, the truth of suffering, origination, cessation, and path; how is the threefold root-reality the truth of suffering and so on? Because it has the marks beginning with impermanence,

children.translated_text: Therefore it is held to be the truth of suffering,

body.translated_text: By the threefold sense of origination, it is the truth of origination; the three senses of origination are:

children.text: vāsanātha samutthānam avisaṃyoga eva ca // III.8
children.translated_text: Disposition (<s>vāsanā</s>), and arisal, and also non-disjunction, III.8

body.text: vāsanāsamudayaḥ parikalpitasvabhāvābhiniveśavāsanā samutthānasamudayaḥ karmakleśāḥ / avisaṃyogasamudayaḥ / tathatāyā āvaraṇāvisaṃyogaḥ / trividhena nirodhena nirodhasatyaṃ [/] trividho nirodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Origination as disposition is the disposition of fixation on the <s>parikalpita</s>-nature; origination as arisal is action-and-afflictions (<s>karma</s>-<s>kleśa</s>); origination as non-disjunction is the non-disjunction of the veiling of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>); by the threefold cessation, it is the truth of cessation; the threefold cessation is:
The non-arising of the two natures, and what is called the twofold pacification of stains,

body.text: svabhāvānutpattir grāhyagrāhakayor anutpattir malaśāntidvayaṃ ca pratisaṃkhyānirodhatathatākhyam ity eṣa trividho nirodho yad uta svabhāvanirodho dvayanirodhaḥ / prakṛtinirodhaś ca / mārgasatyaṃ trividhe mūlatatve kathaṃ vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: Non-arising of own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), non-arising of the apprehended and apprehender (<s>grāhya</s>-<s>grāhaka</s>), and the twofold pacification of stains (<s>mala-śānti-dvaya</s>)—this is called cessation through analytic discernment and suchness (<s>pratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s>-<s>tathatā</s>-designated); this is the threefold cessation, namely: cessation of own-nature, the twofold cessation, and natural (intrinsic) cessation (<s>prakṛti-nirodha</s>); how is the truth of path established within the threefold root-reality?

children.text: parijñāyāṃ prahāṇe ca prāptisākṣātkṛtāv ayaṃ [//] III.9
children.translated_text: In full understanding and in abandonment, and in attainment and direct realization—this [is the way], III.9
Mvbh 41
The truth of path is thus declared,

body.text: parikalpitasya parijñāne paratantrasya parijñāne prahāṇe ca / pariniṣpannasya parijñāne prāptisākṣātkaraṇe ca evam atra parijñāprahāṇasākṣātkriyāyāṃ mārgasatyavyavasthānam iti veditavyaṃ [/]
body.translated_text: By the full understanding of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>), and by the full understanding and abandonment of the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>); and by the full understanding and the making-manifest of attainment with respect to the perfectly accomplished (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>)—thus here, in the acts of full understanding, abandonment, and direct realization, the establishment of the truth of path is to be understood
5. Coarse-and-subtle-reality

body.text: audārikasūkṣmatatvaṃ punaḥ saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyaṃ tan mūlatatve kathaṃ veditavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Coarse-and-subtle reality is again the conventional and the ultimate truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>-<s>paramārtha</s>-satya); how is that to be understood within root-reality?

children.translated_text: By designation and by practical attainment, and by elicitation it is coarse,

body.text: trividhā hi saṃvṛtiḥ prajñaptisaṃvṛtiḥ / pratipattisaṃvṛtiḥ / udbhāvanāsaṃvṛtiś ca / tayā saṃvṛtisatyatvaṃ mūlatatve yathākramaṃ veditavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: For the conventional is threefold: convention of designation (<s>prajñapti-saṃvṛti</s>), convention of practical attainment (<s>pratipatti-saṃvṛti</s>), and convention of elicitation (<s>udbhāvanā-saṃvṛti</s>); by that, conventional truth, within root-reality, is to be understood in due order

children.translated_text: But the ultimate is from the one alone, III.10

body.text: paramārthasatyaṃ / ekasmāt pariniṣpannād eva svabhāvād veditavyaṃ / sa punaḥ kathaṃ paramārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Ultimate truth is to be understood from one own-nature only, namely from the perfectly accomplished (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>)—how, then, is that the ultimate?
For the ultimate is considered threefold by way of object, attainment, and practice

body.text: arthaparamārthas tathatā paramasya jñānasyārtha iti kṛtvā / prāptiparamārtho nirvāṇaṃ paramo 'rtha iti kṛtvā pratipattiparamārtho mārgaḥ paramo 'syārtha iti kṛtvā [/] katham asaṃskṛtaṃ ca (/) saṃskṛtaṃ ca (/) pariniṣpannaḥ (/) svabhāva ucyate /
body.translated_text: Object-ultimate is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), taken as the object of supreme knowledge; attainment-ultimate is <s>nirvāṇa</s> (extinction), taken as the supreme aim; practice-ultimate is the path, taken as its supreme aim; how, then, is the perfectly accomplished own-nature said to be both the unconditioned and the conditioned?

children.translated_text: By completion as non-modification and as non-inversion, the twofold [division arises], III.11

body.text: asaṃskṛtam avikārapariniṣpattyā pariniṣpannaṃ / saṃskṛtaṃ mārgasatyasaṃgṛhītam aviparyāsapariniṣpattyā punar jñeyavastuny

children.translated_text: Mvbh 42
because of non-inversion

body.translated_text: The unconditioned is perfectly accomplished by completion as non-modification; the conditioned, embraced by the truth of path, is, with respect to the knowable object, perfectly accomplished again by completion as non-inversion,
6. Established-reality

body.text: prasiddhatatvaṃ mūlatatve kathaṃ vyavasthāpyate / dvividhaṃ hi prasiddhatatvaṃ / lokaprasiddhaṃ yuktiprasiddhaṃ ca / tatra /
body.translated_text: How is established-reality to be set forth within root-reality? Established-reality is twofold: established by the world and established by reasoning; therein,

children.translated_text: What is established by the world is from one [source],

body.text: parikalpitasvabhāvāt / yasmin vastuni saṃketasaṃstavānupraviṣṭayā buddhyā sarveṣāṃ laukikānāṃ darśanatulyatā bhavati / pṛthivy eveyaṃ nāgnī rūpam evedaṃ na śabda ity evamādi /
body.translated_text: namely from the imagined own-nature (<s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s>): in that existent, by a cognition imbued with conventional assignment and collective approval, there is a likeness of seeing for all worldlings; “this indeed is earth, not fire; this indeed is form, not sound,” and so forth,
What is established by reasoning is from the three,

body.text: yat satāṃ yuktārthapaṇḍitānāṃ tārkikāṇāṃ pramāṇatrayaṃ niśrityopapattisādhanayuktyā prasiddhaṃ vastu /
body.translated_text: namely: that existent which, relying on the three means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa-traya</s>), is established by the inferential proof of reasoning by the wise who are skilled in sound meaning, the logicians
7. Domain-of-purification-reality

body.text: viśuddhigocaratatvaṃ dvividhaṃ kleśāvaraṇaviśuddhijñānagocaraṃ / jñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhijñānagocaraṃ ca / tad etat /
body.translated_text: The domain-of-purification-reality is twofold: the domain of the knowledge of purification with respect to the obstruction of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa-viśuddhi-jñāna-gocara</s>), and the domain of the knowledge of purification with respect to the obstruction of what is to be known (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa-viśuddhi-jñāna-gocara</s>); this

children.text: viśuddhigocaraṃ dvedhā ekasmād eva kīrtitaṃ // III.12
children.translated_text: Domain-of-purification is proclaimed as twofold from the one alone, III.12

body.text: pariniṣpannād eva svabhāvān na hy anyasvabhāvo viśuddhijñānadvayagocaro bhavati /
body.translated_text: namely from the perfectly accomplished own-nature (<s>pariniṣpanna-svabhāva</s>) alone; for no other own-nature becomes the domain of the twofold knowledge of purification
8. Comprehensive-reality
How is comprehensive-reality to be understood within the threefold root-reality?
There is a twofold comprehending, of mark (objective condition) and of conceptual construction, and also of name,

body.text: yathāyogaṃ pañca vastūny ārabhya nimittavikalpayoḥ paratantreṇa

children.translated_text: Mvbh 43

body.translated_text: Beginning, as applicable, with the five things, there is, by the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), a comprehending of mark and of conceptual construction; and of name, by the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>)

children.translated_text: And there is, of the reality of right knowledge alone, a single comprehending, III.13

body.translated_text: namely, by the perfectly accomplished own-nature (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) there is the comprehending of suchness and right knowledge
9. Differentiated-reality

body.text: prabhedatatvaṃ mūlatatve kathaṃ veditavyaṃ / saptavidhaṃ prabhedatatvaṃ pravṛttitatvaṃ / lakṣaṇatatvaṃ / vijñaptitatvaṃ sanniveśatatvaṃ / mithyāpratipattitatvaṃ / viśuddhitatvaṃ samyakpratipattitatvañ ca / (tatra pravṛttitatvāditrividhaṃ / anavarāgreṣv eti saṃsāraḥ tathatācittasaṃkleśāt satvāḥ saṃkliśyanta iti sarvaṃ duḥkhādisatyaṃ ca yathāsaṃkhyaṃ) yaiva ca sandhinirmocanasūtre saptavidhā tathatā nirdiṣṭā / tatra /
body.translated_text: How is differentiated-reality to be understood within root-reality? Differentiated-reality is sevenfold: activity-reality, mark-reality, manifestation-reality, arrangement-reality, false-practice-reality, purification-reality, and right-practice-reality; and therein the triad beginning with activity-reality: “In the beginningless [stream], saṃsāra goes on; from the defilement of mind vis-à-vis <s>tathatā</s>, beings are defiled”—and likewise all the truth beginning with suffering, in due order; and moreover, in the <s>Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra</s>, the sevenfold suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) is taught; therein,
Activity-reality is twofold,

body.text: mūlatatvaṃ veditavyaṃ / parikalpitaparatantralakṣaṇaṃ / yathā pravṛttitatvaṃ tathā /
body.translated_text: Root-reality is to be understood, as having the marks of the imagined and the other-dependent, just as [there is] activity-reality so also
the arrangement and the manifestation,
even with respect to arrangement-reality and false-practice-reality, in just the same way there is a twofold root-reality,

children.translated_text: one [more] is the right-practice of purity in respect of manifestation and of mark, III.14

body.translated_text: The realities beginning with mark-reality are four; a single root-reality is the perfectly accomplished mark,
Mvbh 44
10. Skill-reality

body.text: kauśalyatatvaṃ darśanapratipakṣeṇety uktaṃ / katham eṣu skandhādiṣu daśavidham ātmadarśanam /
body.translated_text: Skill-reality (<s>kauśalya-tattva</s>) is said to be by way of the antidote to views; how is there the tenfold self-view with respect to these [aggregates] beginning with the <s>skandhas</s>?

children.translated_text: As [consisting in] unity, [as] causality, [as] enjoyership, [as] agenthood, [as] sovereignty,
as lordship, as having the meaning of permanence, and even as basis of defilement and of purification, III.15

body.translated_text: as being a <s>yogin</s>, and as being unliberated-and-liberated—such is the seeing of self in these indeed,

body.text: eṣa daśavidha ātmāsadgrāhaḥ skandhādiṣu pravartate / yasya pratipakṣeṇa daśavidhaṃ kauśalyaṃ yad utaikatvagrāho hetutvagrāho bhoktṛtvagrāhaḥ / kartṛtvagrāhaḥ / svatantragrāhaḥ i adhipatitvagrāho nityatvagrāhaḥ / saṃkliṣṭavyavadānatvagrāho yogitvagrāhaḥ / amuktamuktatvagrāhaś ca /
body.translated_text: This tenfold grasping of a non-existent self operates in the <s>skandhas</s> and so on; over against it, the tenfold skill is as follows, namely: the grasping of unity, the grasping of causality, the grasping of enjoyership, the grasping of agenthood, the grasping of independence, the grasping of overlordship, the grasping of permanence, the grasping that [takes them as] defiled-and-purified, the grasping of being a <s>yogin</s>, and the grasping of being both unliberated and liberated

body.text: katham idaṃ daśavidhaṃ kauśalyatatvaṃ mūlatatve 'ntarbhavati / yatas triṣu svabhāveṣu te skandhādayo 'ntarbhūtāḥ / katham antarbhūtāḥ /
body.translated_text: How does this tenfold skill-reality fall within root-reality? Because the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest are included within the three natures; how are they included?

children.translated_text: By the fact that, with respect to them, there is imagined, discriminated, and dharmatā-character, III.16

body.text: trividhaṃ rūpaṃ parikalpitaṃ rūpaṃ yo rūpasya parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ / vikalpitaṃ rūpaṃ yo rūpasya paratantraḥ (/) svabhāvas tatra hi rūpavikalpaḥ kriyate / dharmatārūpaṃ yo rūpasya pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ / yathā rūpam evaṃ vedanādayaḥ skandhāḥ dhātvāyatanādayaś ca yojyāḥ / evan triṣu svabhāveṣu skandhādīnām antarbhāvād daśavidhaṃ kauśalyatatvaṃ mūlatatva eva draṣṭavyaṃ / uktam idaṃ yathā daśavidhātmadarśanapratipakṣeṇa skandhādikauśalyaṃ [/] skandhādyarthas tu noktaḥ / sa idānīm ucyate/
body.translated_text: The threefold form: imagined form—namely, that which is the imagined own-nature of form; discriminated form—namely, that which is the other-dependent own-nature of form, for there, discrimination of form is effected; dharmatā-form—namely, that which is the perfectly accomplished own-nature of form; just as with form, so the <s>skandhas</s> beginning with feeling, and likewise the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>, are to be applied; thus, because the <s>skandhas</s> and so on are included in the three natures, the tenfold skill-reality is to be seen precisely within root-reality; this has been stated concerning the skill regarding the <s>skandhas</s> as the antidote to the tenfold self-view; but the object of the <s>skandhas</s> has not been stated—this now is stated
Mvbh 45
a. Object of the <s>skandhas</s>
For the sake of the meanings of plurality, of summary, and of delimitation, first,

body.text: āditas tāvat skandhās te trividhenārthena veditavyāḥ / anekatvārthena yat kiñcid rūpam atītānāgatapratyutpannam iti vistaraḥ / abhisaṃkṣepārthena tat sarvam aikadhyam abhisaṃkṣipyeti / paricchedārthena ca rūpādilakṣaṇasya pṛthaktvavyavasthānāt / rāśyartho hi skandhārtha evaṃ ca loke rāśyartho dṛṣṭa iti /
body.translated_text: First of all, the <s>skandhas</s> are to be understood by a threefold meaning: by the meaning of plurality—namely, whatever form, whether past, future, or present, and so on in detail; by the meaning of summary—namely, all that is gathered into a unity in summary form; and by the meaning of delimitation—namely, because of the distinct determination of the mark of form and so on; for heap-meaning indeed is the very meaning of skandha, and thus in the world the heap-meaning is seen
b. Object of the <s>dhātus</s>
Another [meaning] is taught: the meaning of apprehender, of apprehended, and of the seed of that apprehension, III.17

body.text: katamo 'paro dhātus tatra grāhakabījārthaḥ cakṣurdhātvādayaḥ [/] grāhyabījārtho rūpadhātvādayas [/] tadgrāhabījārthaś cakṣurvijñānadhātvādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the other, the <s>dhātu</s>? Therein, the seed-meaning of the apprehender is the eye-<s>dhātu</s> and so on; the seed-meaning of the apprehended is the form-<s>dhātu</s> and so on; the seed-meaning of that apprehension is the eye-consciousness-<s>dhātu</s> and so on
c. Object of the <s>āyatanas</s>
Another [meaning is given] from the doors of knowing, delimitation of objects, and enjoyment,

body.text: kim aparaṃ āyatanaṃ / tatra veditopabhogāyadvārārthena ṣaḍ ādhyātmikāny āyatanāni / arthaparicchedopabhogāyadvārārthena ṣaḍ bāhyāni /
body.translated_text: What is the other, the <s>āyatana</s>? Therein, by the meaning of door for knowing and enjoying, the six internal <s>āyatanas</s>; and by the meaning of door for delimitation of objects and enjoying, the six external [<s>āyatanas</s>]
d. Object of dependent arising
The object of dependent arising (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>),

children.translated_text: Again—by way of the non-superimposition and non-denial of cause, fruit, and activity, III.18

body.text: hetuphalakriyāṇām asamāropānapavādārthaḥ pratītyasamutpādārthaḥ / tatra hetu sa nāropaḥ saṃskārādīnāṃ viṣamahetukalpanāt /

children.translated_text: Mvbh 46

children.text: hetvapavādo nirhetukatvakalpanāt phalasamāropaḥ sātmakānāṃ saṃskārādīnām avidyādipratyayapravṛttikalpanāt / phalāpavādo na santy avidyādipratyayāḥ saṃskārādaya iti kalpanāt / kriyāsamāropo 'vidyādīnāṃ saṃskārādyutpattau vyāpārakalpanāt kriyāpavādo niḥsāmarthyakalpanāt tadabhāvād asamāropānapavādo veditavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: cause-negation is from imagining their being without cause; fruit-superimposition is from imagining that conditioned factors, which are with self, proceed by the condition that is ignorance and so on; fruit-negation is from imagining, “there are no conditions such as ignorance for formations and so on”; activity-superimposition is from imagining an operation for ignorance and so on in the production of formations and so on; activity-negation is from imagining their lack of capacity; by the absence of these, non-superimposition and non-denial are to be understood

body.translated_text: The object of dependent arising is the meaning of non-superimposition and non-denial with respect to causes, fruits, and activities; therein, cause—there is non-superimposition, from rejecting the imagining of the conditioned factors such as formations as having disparate causes,
e. Object of what is fitting and unfitting
Another [meaning is given] by way of the simultaneous arising and lordship of the undesirable, the desirable, and the pure; and by way of attainment, conventional practice, and dependence, III.19

body.text: sthānāsthānaṃ saptavidhapāratantryārthena veditavyaṃ / tatrāniṣṭe pāratantryaṃ duścaritenānicchato 'pi durgatigamanād iṣṭe pāratantryaṃ sucaritena sugatigamanāt / viśuddhau pāratantryaṃ pañca nivaraṇāny aprahāya yāvat saptabodhyaṅgāny abhāvayitvā duḥkhasyāntākaraṇāt samotpattau pāratantryaṃ dvayor apūrvācaramayos tathāgatayoś cakravartinoś caikasmin lokadhātāv anutpādād ādhipatye pāratantryaṃ striyāś cakravartitvādyakaraṇāt saṃprāptau pāratantryaṃ striyāḥ pratyekānuttarabodhyanabhisaṃbodhāt samudācāre pāratantryaṃ dṛṣṭisaṃpannasya vadhādyupakramāsamudācārāt pṛthagjanasya ca samudācārād vistareṇa bahudhātukasūtrānusārād anugantavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: What is fitting and unfitting (sthānāsthāna) is to be understood by the sevenfold meaning of dependence (<s>pāratantrya</s>): therein, in the undesirable there is dependence, because, even for one who does not wish it due to bad conduct, there is going to a bad destiny; in the desirable there is dependence, because from good conduct there is going to a good destiny; in purity there is dependence, because, without abandoning the five hindrances and without cultivating up to the seven factors of awakening, there is making an end of suffering; in simultaneous arising there is dependence, because, for the two unprecedented practitioners, namely a <s>Tathāgata</s> and a wheel-turning monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>), there is non-arising in a single world-system; in lordship there is dependence, because a woman does not effect wheel-turning-monarchy and so on; in attainment there is dependence, because a woman does not perfectly awaken to the individually-supreme unsurpassed awakening; in conventional practice there is dependence, because one possessed of view-attainment does not undertake procedures such as killing, whereas an ordinary person does undertake them—this should be followed out in detail in accordance with the Many-Factors Sūtra (<s>Bahudhātuka-sūtra</s>)
f. The domain of the faculties (<s>indriyārtha</s>)
The faculty (<s>indriya</s>) moreover is of twenty-two kinds,
by the meanings of apprehension, of locus, of conjunction, of enjoyment, and of the twofold purity,
Mvbh 47

body.text: grahaṇārthena yāvad viśuddhidvayārthena teṣu tadādhipatyād rūpādiviṣayagrahaṇe hi cakṣurādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇām ādhipatyaṃ sthāne jīvitendriyasya tadādhipatyenāmaraṇāt / kulasandhāne strīpuruṣendriyayor apatyaprasavādhipatyād upabhoge vedanendriyāṇāṃ kuśalākuśalakarmaphalopabhogāt / laukikaviśuddhau śraddhādīnāṃ / lokottaraviśuddhau anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyādīnāṃ /
body.translated_text: By the meaning of apprehension—up to by the meaning of the twofold purity—among these, because of their lordship therein: for, in the apprehension of objects such as form, there is lordship of the six beginning with the eye; in locus, there is the life-faculty’s lordship, because, through its authority, there is non-dying; in conjunction of family, there is the lordship of the female and male faculties, because of procreation of offspring; in enjoyment, there is the experience of the fruit of wholesome and unwholesome karma by the feeling-faculties; in worldly purity, those such as faith; in supramundane purity, those such as “I will know what has not been known” faculty,
g. The domain of temporal series (<s>adhvārtha</s>)
Because of the meanings of fruit, cause, applicability, and non-applicability, thereafter another, III.20

body.text: kim aparam adhvatrayaṃ yathāyogaṃ phalahetūpayogārthenātīto 'dhvā phalahetvanupayogārthenānāgato 'dhvā hetūpayogaphalānupayogārthena pratyutpanno 'dhvā veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the other, the threefold temporal series (<s>adhvatraya</s>)? As applicable, by the meaning of fruit-and-cause non-applicability, the past temporal series is to be understood; by the meaning of cause-applicability and fruit-non-applicability, the future temporal series; by the meaning of applicability of cause and non-applicability of fruit, the present temporal series
h. The domain of the Four Truths (<s>catuḥsatyārtha</s>)
By the meanings of feeling, sign of feeling, and attainment of that sign; by the fitness for the meaning of pacification and of antidote, another is approved, III.21

body.text: kim aparaṃ satyacatuṣṭayaṃ / tatra duḥkhasatyaṃ vedanāsanimittārthena yat kiñcid veditam idam atra duḥkhasyeti kṛtvā vedanānimittaṃ punar vedanāsthānīyā dharmā veditavyāḥ / tannimittapratipattitaḥ samudayasatyaṃ duḥkhasatyanimittaṃ yā pratipattiḥ / tayoḥ śamārthena nirodhasatyaṃ / pratipakṣārthena mārgasatyaṃ /
body.translated_text: What is the other, the fourfold truth? Therein, the truth of suffering is by the meaning of feeling and of the sign of feeling—whatever is to be understood as “this here is of suffering,” making it thus; again, by “sign of feeling” the dharmas standing in the place of feeling are to be understood; by the attainment of that sign, the truth of origin, namely whatever attainment there is of the sign of the truth of suffering; of those two, by the meaning of pacification, the truth of cessation; by the meaning of antidote, the truth of path
i. The domain of the three vehicles (<s>yānatrayārtha</s>)

body.text:
guṇadoṣāvikalpena jñānena parataḥ svayaṃ [/]
niryāṇād aparaṃ jñeyaṃ /
body.translated_text: By knowledge discriminating qualities and faults with respect to nirvāṇa and <s>saṃsāra</s>, by what is heard from another or by oneself, and by going forth, another is to be known,
Mvbh 48

body.text: yānatrayaṃ yathāyogaṃ / tatra nirvāṇasaṃsārayor guṇadoṣajñānena parataḥ (/) śrutvā niryāṇārthena śrāvakayānaṃ / tenaiva svayam aśrutvā parato niryāṇārthena pratyekabuddhayānaṃ / avikalpena jñānena svayaṃ niryāṇārthena mahāyānaṃ veditavyaṃ //
body.translated_text: The three vehicles, as applicable: therein, by knowledge of the qualities and faults of <s>nirvāṇa</s> and <s>saṃsāra</s>, from another—having heard—and by the meaning of going forth, the <s>śrāvaka-yāna</s>; by that very [knowledge], without having heard oneself from another, by the meaning of going forth, the <s>pratyekabuddha-yāna</s>; by non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>) knowledge, by oneself, by the meaning of going forth, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is to be understood
j. The domain of conditioned and unconditioned (<s>saṃskṛta-asaṃskṛtārtha</s>)

body.text:
saprajñaptisahetukāt /
nimittāt praśamāt sārthāt paścimaṃ samudāhṛtaṃ // III.22
body.translated_text: From imputation, from cause, from sign, from pacification, from what has meaning, the last is set forth, III.22

body.text: saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaṃ tatra saprajñaptir nāmakāyādayaḥ hetur bījasaṃgṛhītam ālayavijñānaṃ / nimittaṃ pratiṣṭhādehabhogasaṃgṛhītaṃ / pravṛttivijñānasaṃgṛhītāś ca manaudgrahavikalpaḥ / etat saprajñaptisahetukaṃ nimittaṃ sasaṃprayogaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ veditavyaṃ / tatra mano yan nityaṃ manyanākāraṃ / udgrahaḥ pañcavijñānakāyāḥ vikalpo manovijñānaṃ (/) tasya vikalpakatvād asaṃskṛtaṃ punaḥ praśamaś ca nirodhaḥ / praśamārthaś ca tathatā tatra praśamo nirodho mārgaś ca yaś ca praśamo yena ceti kṛtvā praśamārthaḥ tathatā praśamasyārtha iti kṛtvā tathatāyā mārgālambanatvāt / mārgasya praśamatvan tena praśamanāt /
body.translated_text: Conditioned and unconditioned—therein, imputation (<s>prajñapti</s>) is name-aggregate and the like; cause is the store-consciousness (<s>ālaya-vijñāna</s>) that includes seeds; sign is what is included in the support-body and enjoyments; and grasping-up and conceptual construction included in the functioning consciousnesses—this complex of sign with associated factors, having imputation and cause, is to be understood as conditioned; therein, manas is that which constantly has the mode of conceiving, grasping-up is the fivefold consciousness-group, conceptual construction is mind-consciousness—because of its being conceptual, that is unconditioned? Rather, pacification (<s>praśama</s>) is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>); and the meaning of pacification is suchness (<s>tathatā</s>): there, taking pacification as cessation and path, and that by which there is pacification, making “meaning of pacification” to be suchness—the meaning of pacification—therefore, because suchness has the path as its support, and because the path has the character of pacification, therefore from pacification

body.text: ity etenārthena skandhādiṣu jñānaṃ skandhādikauśalyaṃ veditavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: By this meaning, knowledge regarding the <s>skandhas</s> and so on, and skill regarding the <s>skandhas</s> and so on, is to be understood
Summary of the import of the realities

body.text: tatvasya piṇḍārthaḥ / samāsato dvividhaṃ tatvaṃ / ādarśatatvaṃ / dṛśyatatvaṃ ca tatrādarśatatvaṃ mūlatatvaṃ tatra śeṣāṇāṃ darśanāt /
body.translated_text: The gist of the realities (<s>tattvapiṇḍārtha</s>): in brief, the reality (<s>tattva</s>) is twofold: mirror-reality (<s>ādarśa-tattva</s>) and seen-reality (<s>dṛśya-tattva</s>); among these, mirror-reality is root-reality (<s>mūla-tattva</s>), because the remainder are seen by it,
Mvbh 49

body.text: dṛśyatatvaṃ navavidhaṃ nirabhimānadṛśyatatvaṃ / aviparyāsadṛśyatatvaṃ / śrāvakayānaniryāṇadṛśyatatvaṃ / mahāyānaniryāṇadṛśyatatvaṃ / audārikeṇa paripācanāt / sūkṣmeṇa ca vimocanāt paravādinigrahadṛśyatatvaṃ / dṛṣṭāntasanniśrayeṇa yuktyā nigrahāt / mahāyānābhidyotanadṛśyatatvaṃ / sarvākārajñeyapraveśadṛśyatatvaṃ / avitathatathatābhidyotanadṛśyatatvaṃ / ātmagrāhavastusarvābhisandhipraveśadṛśyatatvaṃ ca // ḥ //
body.translated_text: Seen-reality is ninefold: seen-reality of non-conceit; seen-reality of non-inversion; seen-reality of going forth by the <s>Śrāvaka-yāna</s>; seen-reality of going forth by the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; seen-reality of refutation of opposing doctrines, through ripening by the gross and release by the subtle; seen-reality of refutation by reasoning, on the basis of reliance on examples; seen-reality of the illumination of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; seen-reality of entry into the knowable in all modes (<s>sarvākāra-jñeya-praveśa</s>); seen-reality of the illumination of unfailing suchness (<s>avitatha-tathatā</s>); and also seen-reality of entry into all intentional engagements with respect to the real entity of self-grasping,
In the treatise <s>Madhyāntavibhāga-śāstra</s>, the third [chapter] is the delimitation of reality (<s>tattva-pariccheda</s>)
Mvbh 50
CHAPTER IV. Determination of the cultivation of the antidotes, the stages, and the fruits
[1. Cultivation of the antidotes]
The cultivation of the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanā</s>)—the cultivation belonging to the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya-bhāvanā</s>)—is now to be stated,
a. The four establishments of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)
Therein, first of all,

children.text:
dauṣṭhulyāt tarṣahetutvād vastutvād avimohataḥ /
catuḥsatyāvatārāya smṛtyupasthānabhāvanā // IV.1
children.translated_text: Because of coarseness, because of being the cause of thirst, because of being a real entity, and because of non-delusion, for the introduction to the Four Truths, there is the cultivation of the establishments of mindfulness, IV.1

body.text: kāyena hi dauṣṭhulyaṃ prabhāvyate / tatparīkṣayā duḥkhasatyam avatarati / tasya sadauṣṭhulyasaṃskāralakṣaṇatvāt / dauṣṭhulyaṃ hi saṃskāraduḥkhatā / tayā sarvaṃ sāsravaṃ vastv āryā duḥkhataḥ paśyantīti / tṛṣṇāhetur vedanā tatparīkṣayā samudayasatyam avatarati / ātmābhiniveśavastu cittaṃ tatparīkṣayā nirodhasatyam avataraty ātmocchedabhayāpagamāt / dharmaparīkṣayā sāṃkleśikavaiyavadānikadharmāsaṃmohāt / mārgasatyam avataraty ataḥ (/) ādau catuḥsatyāvatārāya smṛtyupasthānabhāvanā vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: For coarseness is made prominent by the body; by its examination the truth of suffering is entered, because it has the characteristic of being formed with perpetual coarseness; for coarseness is the painfulness-of-formations—by that the noble ones see all that is with outflows as of the nature of suffering; feeling is the cause of thirst—by its examination the truth of origin is entered; mind, the real entity of clinging to self, by its examination the truth of cessation is entered, due to the removal of the fear of annihilation of self; by the examination of dharmas, through non-delusion regarding defiled and purified dharmas, the truth of the path is entered therefore, to begin with, for the introduction to the Four Truths, the cultivation of the establishments of mindfulness is laid down,
b. The four right abandonings (<s>samyak-prahāṇa</s>)
Then, the cultivation of right abandoning—for,

children.text:
parijñāte vipakṣe ca pratipakṣe ca sarvathā /
tadapāyāyavīryaṃ hi caturdhā saṃpravartate // IV.2
children.translated_text: When the contrary and the antidote have been fully known in every way, energy for their removal indeed proceeds in four ways, IV.2

body.text: smṛtyupasthānabhāvanayā vipakṣe pratipakṣe ca sarvaprakāraṃ parijñāte vipakṣāpagamāya pratipakṣopagamāya ca vīryañ caturdhā saṃpravartate / utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāyeti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: By the cultivation of the establishments of mindfulness, when the contrary and the antidote have been fully known in all modes, energy proceeds fourfold for the removal of the contrary and the approach of the antidote—namely, for the abandoning of arisen evil unwholesome dharmas, and so forth in detail,
Mvbh 51
c. The four bases of success (<s>ṛddhi-pāda</s>)

body.text:
karmaṇyatā sthites tatra sarvārthānāṃ samṛddhaye /
pañcadoṣaprahāṇāṣṭasaṃskārāsevanānvayā // IV.3
body.translated_text: When there is fitness of mind established there, for the accomplishment of all aims, through the abandoning of the five faults and the cultivation of the eight trainings, it follows, IV.3

body.text: tasyāṃ tadapāyāyavīryabhāvanāyāṃ cittasthiteḥ (/) karmaṇyatā catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ sarvārthasamṛddhihetutvāt sthitir atra cittasthitiḥ samādhir veditavyaḥ / ataḥ samyakprahāṇānantaram ṛddhipādāḥ / sā punaḥ karmaṇyatā pañcadoṣaprahāṇāyāṣṭaprahāṇasaṃskārabhāvanānvayā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: When in that cultivation of energy for their removal there is stability of mind, there is fitness (<s>karmaṇyatā</s>): the four bases of success are set forth, because they are the cause of the accomplishment of all aims; here, “stability” of mind is to be understood as concentration (<s>samādhi</s>); therefore, after the right abandonings, [come] the bases of success; and that fitness, moreover, is to be understood as following upon the abandoning of the five faults and the cultivation of the eight trainings of abandoning,
The five faults (<s>pañca doṣāḥ</s>)
Which are the five faults? He says:

children.text:
kausīdyam avavādasya saṃmoṣo laya uddhataḥ /
asaṃskāro 'tha saṃskāraḥ pañca doṣā ime matāḥ // IV.4
children.translated_text: Sloth (<s>kausīdya</s>), disparagement (<s>avavāda</s>), loss (forgetfulness) (<s>saṃmoṣa</s>), sinking (<s>laya</s>), excitement (<s>uddhata</s>), non-preparation (<s>asaṃskāra</s>), and then preparation (<s>saṃskāra</s>)—these five faults are considered, IV.4

body.text: tatra layauddhatyam eko doṣaḥ kriyate / anabhisaṃskāro layauddhatyapraśamanakāle doṣaḥ / abhisaṃskāraḥ praśāntau [/]
body.translated_text: Therein, sinking-and-excitement are taken as one fault; non-preparation is the fault at the time of not pacifying sinking and excitement; preparation is [a fault] at the time of pacification,
The eight trainings for abandoning (<s>aṣṭa prahāṇa-saṃskārāḥ</s>)

body.text: eṣāṃ prahāṇāya katham aṣṭau prahāṇasaṃskārā vyavasthāpyante / catvāraḥ kausīdyaprahāṇāya cchandavyāyāmaśraddhāprasrabdhayas te punar yathākramaṃ veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: For the abandoning of these, how are the eight trainings for abandoning established? Four are for the abandoning of sloth: zeal (<s>chanda</s>), energy (<s>vyāyāma</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and pliancy (<s>prasrabdhi</s>)—and these are to be understood, further, in due order,

body.text: āśrayo 'thāśritas tasya nimittaṃ phalam eva ca /
body.translated_text: Support, and that which depends on the support, its sign, and the result as well,

body.text: āśrayaś chando vyāyāmasya / āśrito vyāyāmas tasyāśrayasya cchandasya nimittaṃ śraddhā saṃpratyaye (/) saty abhilāṣāt tasyāśritasya vyāyāmasya phalaṃ prasrabdhir ārabdhavīryasya samādhiviśeṣādhigamāc

children.translated_text: Mvbh 52

children.text: cheṣāś catvāraḥ prahāṇasaṃskārāḥ smṛtisaṃprajanyacetanopekṣāś caturṇāṃ doṣāṇāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ pratipakṣās te punaḥ smṛtyādayo veditavyā yathākramaṃ /
children.translated_text: The remaining four trainings for abandoning are mindfulness, clear comprehension, intention, and equanimity; these are, respectively, the antidotes to the four faults in due order; and again, those beginning with mindfulness should be understood in sequence,

body.translated_text: The support is zeal; energy depends on the support; the sign of that support—of zeal—is faith, on the ascertainment, due to aspiration for the truth; the result of that dependent energy is pliancy, for one who has initiated vigor, because of the attainment of a special concentration,

children.text:
ālambane 'saṃmoṣo layauddhatyānubuddhyanā /
tadapāyābhisaṃskāraḥ śāntau praśaṭhavāhitā // IV.5
children.translated_text: Non-forgetfulness with respect to the object; the discerning of sinking and excitement; the formation (cultivation) for the removal of that; in pacification, smooth flowing-guidance—IV.5

body.text: smṛtir ālambane 'saṃpramoṣaḥ saṃprajanyaṃ smṛtyasaṃpramoṣe sati layauddhatyānubodhaḥ / anubudhya tadapagamāyābhisaṃskāraś cetanā / tasya layauddhatyasyopaśāntau satyāṃ praśaṭhavāhitā cittasyopekṣā [/]
body.translated_text: Mindfulness is non-lapse with respect to the object; clear comprehension is the discerning of sinking and excitement when there is non-lapse of mindfulness; having discerned, intention is the formation (cultivation) for the removal of that; when there is pacification of that sinking and excitement, equanimity is the mind’s smooth flowing-guidance [ ]
d. The five faculties (<s>pañcendriyāṇi</s>)

body.text: ṛddhipādānām anantaraṃ pañcendriyāṇi śraddhādīni teṣāṃ kathaṃ vyavasthānaṃ /
body.translated_text: Immediately after the bases of success, the five faculties beginning with faith—how is their arrangement?

children.text:
ropite mokṣabhāgīye cchandayogādhipatyataḥ /
ālambane 'saṃmoṣāvisāravicayasya ca // IV.6
children.translated_text: When the liberation-partaking wholesome root has been established, through the mastery of zeal and of application; and of non-forgetfulness with respect to the object; and of non-diffusion; and of investigation—IV.6

body.text: ādhipatyata iti vartate / ṛddhipādaiḥ karmaṇyacittasyāropite mokṣabhāgīye kuśalamūle cchandādhipatyataḥ prayogādhipatyataḥ / ālambanāsaṃpramoṣādhipatyataḥ / avisārādhipatyataḥ / pravicayādhipatyataś ca / yathākramaṃ pañca śraddhādīnīndriyāṇi veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: “Through mastery” continues in sense; when, by the bases of success, the liberation-partaking wholesome root has been established for a mind made fit, then through the mastery of zeal, through the mastery of application, through the mastery of non-lapse with respect to the object, through the mastery of non-diffusion, and through the mastery of investigation, the five faculties beginning with faith should be understood in order,
e. The five powers (<s>pañca balāni</s>)

body.text: tāny eva śraddhādīni balavanti balānīty ucyante / teṣāṃ punar balavatvaṃ
body.translated_text: Those very [five], beginning with faith, being strong are called powers; as for their being strong,
It is indeed by scraping away (attenuation) of the adversary,

body.text: yadā tāny aśraddhādibhir vipakṣair na vyavakīryante / kasmāc chraddhādīnāṃ pūrvottaranirdeśaḥ / yasmāt
body.translated_text: when those [faculties] are not scattered by adversaries such as disbelief; why is there a prior-and-later statement of those beginning with faith? Because
the later is the fruit of the former,

body.text: śraddadhāno hi hetuphalaṃ vīryam ārabhate / ārabdhavīryasya smṛtir upatiṣṭhate / upasthitasmṛteś cittaṃ samādhīyate / samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / avaropitamokṣabhāgīyasyendriyāṇy uktāny atha nirvedhabhāgīyāni kim indriyāvasthāyāṃ veditavyāny āhosvid balāvasthāyāṃ /
body.translated_text: for one who has faith undertakes energy with respect to cause and fruit; for one who has undertaken energy, mindfulness becomes established; when mindfulness is established, the mind becomes concentrated; with a concentrated mind, one knows things as they are; the faculties have been stated for the deposited (established) liberation-partaking [ground], so then, should the penetration-partaking be understood at the level of faculties, or at the level of powers?

children.text: dvau dvau nirvedhabhāgīyāv indriyāṇi balāni ca // IV.7
children.translated_text: Two and two of the penetration-partaking are faculties and powers—IV.7

body.text: uṣmagataṃ mūrdhānaś cendriyāṇi / kṣāntayo laukikāś cāgradharmā balāni /
body.translated_text: The heat and the summit are faculties; the world-transcending forbearances and the supreme qualities are powers,
f. The seven factors of awakening (<s>sapta bodhyaṅgāni</s>)
Immediately after the powers, the awakening-factors—how is their arrangement?

children.text:
āśrayāṅgaṃ svabhāvāṅgaṃ niryāṇāṅgaṃ tṛtīyakaṃ /
caturtham anuśaṃsāṅgan niḥkleśāṅgaṃ tridhā mataṃ // IV.8
children.translated_text: The basis-limb, the nature-limb, the exit-limb, the third; the fourth is the benefit-limb; the non-defilement-limb is taught as threefold—IV.8

body.text: darśanamārge bodhāv aṅgāni bodhyaṅgāni / tatra bodher āśrayāṅgaṃ smṛtiḥ / svabhāvāṅgaṃ dharmavicayaḥ / niryāṇāṅgaṃ vīryaṃ / anuśansāṅgaṃ prītiḥ / asaṃkleśāṅgaṃ tridhā prasrabdhisamādhyupekṣāḥ / kimarthaṃ punar asaṃkleśāṅgaṃ tridhā deśitaṃ
body.translated_text: On the path of seeing, the limbs for awakening are the factors of awakening; therein, mindfulness is the basis-limb of awakening; investigation-of-dharmas is the nature-limb; energy is the exit-limb; rapture is the benefit-limb; the non-defilement-limb is threefold: pliancy, concentration, and equanimity; why, again, is the non-defilement-limb taught as threefold?
Mvbh 54
It is taught here by way of cause, by way of basis, and by way of nature,

body.text: asaṃkleśasya nidānaṃ prasrabdhir dauṣṭhulyahetutvāt saṃkleśasya / tasyāś ca tatpratipakṣatvād āśrayaḥ samādhiḥ / svabhāvaupekṣā [/]
body.translated_text: Pliancy is the cause of non-defilement, because coarseness is the cause of defilement; and concentration is the basis of that, since it is the antidote to it; in nature it is equanimity [ ]
g. The eight factors of the path (<s>aṣṭa mārgāṅgāni</s>)
Immediately after the awakening-factors, the path-factors—how is their arrangement?

children.text:
paricchedo 'tha saṃprāptiḥ parasaṃbhāvanā tridhā [//] IV.9
vipakṣapratipakṣaś ca mārgasyāṅgaṃ tad aṣṭadhā /
children.translated_text: Discrimination, then attainment from others, and approving of others—threefold—IV.9; and the adversary–antidote as the limb of the path is eightfold,

body.text: bhāvanāmārge 'sya paricchedāṅgaṃ samyagdṛṣṭir laukikī lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhā yayā svādhigamaṃ paricchinatti / parasaṃprāpaṇāṅgaṃ samyaksaṃkalpaḥ samyagvāk ca / sasamutthānayā vācā tatprāpaṇāt / parasaṃbhāvanāṅgaṃ tridhā samyagvākkarmāntājīvās tair hi yathākramaṃ /
body.translated_text: On the path of cultivation, right view—worldly and supramundane, obtained subsequently—by which one discriminates one’s own realization—is the discrimination-limb; right intention and right speech are the attainment-from-others limb, because through speech along with its arousal that [attainment from others] is effected; the approving-of-others limb is threefold: right speech, right action, and right livelihood, because, respectively,

children.text: dṛṣṭau śīle 'tha saṃlekhe paravijñaptir iṣyate // IV.10
children.translated_text: approval by others is admitted with regard to view, morality, and refinement,

body.text: tasya samyagvācā kathāsāṃkathyaviniścayena prajñāyāṃ saṃbhāvanā bhavati / samyakkarmāntena śīle 'kṛtyākaraṇāt samyagājīvena saṃlekhe dharmeṇa mātrayā ca cīvarādyanveṣaṇāt / vipakṣapratipakṣāṅgaṃ tridhaiva samyagvyāyamasmṛtisamādhayaḥ / eṣāṃ hi yathākramaṃ /
body.translated_text: for, through right speech, there is approval regarding wisdom by the determination in the discussion of discourses; through right action, regarding morality, by refraining from what ought not be done; through right livelihood, regarding refinement, by a righteous measure and by seeking robe and so on; the adversary–antidote limb is just threefold: right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration; of these, in due order, there is
overcoming of afflictions and subsidiary afflictions, and being the antidote to adversaries,

body.text: trividho hi vipakṣaḥ kleśo bhāvanāheyaḥ / upakleśo layauddhatyaṃ

children.translated_text: Mvbh 55

children.text: vibhutvavipakṣaś ca vaiśeṣikaguṇābhinirhāravibandhaḥ tatra prathamasya samyagvyāyāmaḥ pratipakṣas tena mārgabhāvanāt / dvitīyasya samyaksmṛtiḥ śamathādinimitteṣu sūpasthitasmṛteḥ layauddhatyābhāvāt / tṛtīyasya samyaksamādhiḥ dhyānasanniśrayeṇābhijñādiguṇābhinirhārāt /
children.translated_text: And the adversary of pervasion is the obstruction to the bringing forth of the distinguished qualities of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> [system]; there, for the first, right effort is the antidote, because of the cultivation of the path by it; for the second, right mindfulness, because, with mindfulness well established on the supports such as <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), there is an absence of sinking and excitement; for the third, right concentration, because, relying on the absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), there is the bringing forth of such qualities as superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>),

body.translated_text: for the adversary is threefold: the affliction to be abandoned by cultivation; the subsidiary affliction is sinking–and–excitement
h. The divisions of the cultivation of the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanā-prabheda</s>)
This cultivation of the antidote, in brief, is to be understood as threefold,

children.translated_text: Favorable, inverted, accompanied by a sequel; inverted—IV.11
and non-inverted; and the cultivation not accompanied by the sequel,

body.text: viparyastāpi aviparyāsānukūlāviparyastā viparyāsānubandhā aviparyastā viparyāsaniranubandhā ca yathākramaṃ pṛthagjanaśaikṣāśaikṣāvasthāsu / bodhisatvānān tv
body.translated_text: Even the inverted is: inverted yet favorable to the non-inversion; inverted and accompanied by the inversion as sequel; non-inverted; and non-inverted without the sequel of inversion—these, in due order, in the states of the ordinary person, the learner, and the non-learner; but for the <s>bodhisattvas</s>,

children.translated_text: the attainment of object and attention, and their being distinguished—IV.12

body.text: śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ hi svāsantānikāḥ kāyādayaḥ ālambanam / bodhisatvānāṃ svaparasāntānikāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhā anityādibhir ākāraiḥ kāyādīn manasikurvanti / bodhisatvās tv anupalambhayogena / śrāvakapratyekabuddhāḥ smṛtyupasthānādīni bhāvayanti yāvad eva kāyādīnāṃ visaṃyogāya / bodhisatvā na visaṃyogāya / nāvisaṃyogāya / yāvad evāpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇāya / uktā pratipakṣabhāvanā /
body.translated_text: For the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, the aggregates beginning with body that belong to their own mental continuum are the object; for the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the aggregates beginning with body that belong to their own and to others’ continua; the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> attend to body and so on with modes such as impermanence; but the <s>bodhisattvas</s> by the discipline of non-apprehension; the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> cultivate the establishments of mindfulness and so on only up to the disjunction from body and so on; the <s>bodhisattvas</s> not for disjunction, nor for non-disjunction, but only up to non-abiding nirvāṇa (<s>apratiṣṭhita-nirvāṇa</s>); thus the cultivation of the antidote has been stated,
Mvbh 56

It is named the state of cause, of descent; called application and fruit; and distinguished as what is to be done and what is not to be done; and higher and unsurpassed—IV.13

body.text: tatra hetvavasthā yā gotrasthasya pudgalasyāvatārāvasthā utpāditabodhicittasya prayogāvasthā cittotpādād ūrdham aprāpte phale / phalāvasthā prāpte / sakaraṇīyāvasthā śaikṣasya / akaraṇīyāvasthā aśaikṣasya / viśeṣāvasthābhijñādiguṇaviśeṣasamanvāgatasya / uttarāvasthā śrāvakādibhyo bhūmipraviṣṭasya bodhisatvasya / anuttarāvasthā buddhasya tata ūrdham avasthābhāvād adhimuktyavasthā bodhisatvānāṃ sarvasyām adhimukticaryābhūmau / praveśāvasthā prathamāyāṃ bhūmau niryāṇāvasthā taduttarāsu ṣaṭsu bhūmiṣu / vyākaraṇāvasthā aṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau kathikatvāvasthā navamyām abhiṣekāvasthā daśamyāṃ / prāptyavasthā buddhānān dharmakāyaḥ / anuśansāvasthā sāṃbhogikaḥ kāyaḥ / kṛtyānuṣṭhānāvasthā nirmāṇakāyaḥ / sarvāpy eṣā bahuvidhāvasthābhisamasya veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, the state of cause is the state of the one in the lineage (<s>gotra</s>); the state of descent is the state of one who has produced the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>); the state of application is after the production of mind, before the attainment of the fruit; the state of fruit is at attainment; the state of what is to be done is that of the learner; the state of what is not to be done is that of the non-learner; the state of distinction is that of one endowed with distinctions of qualities such as superknowledges; the higher state is that of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has entered the grounds in distinction from <s>Śrāvakas</s> and so on; the unsurpassed state is that of a Buddha, because beyond that there is no state; the state of decisive resolution is, for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, on the entire level of conduct of decisive resolution; the state of entry is on the first ground; the state of going out is on the six grounds succeeding that; the state of prediction is on the eighth ground; the state of being a preacher is on the ninth; the state of consecration is on the tenth; the state of attainment is the <s>dharmakāya</s> of the Buddhas; the state of commendation is the enjoyment body (<s>sāṃbhogika-kāya</s>); the state of performance of the tasks is the emanation body (<s>nirmāṇa-kāya</s>); all this is to be understood along with many and various states,

children.text:
dharmadhātau tridhā puuaḥ /
aśuddhāśuddhaśuddhā ca viśuddhā ca yathārhataḥ // IV.15
children.translated_text: Again, in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> there are three: impure, impure-pure, and pure; and, as appropriate, purified—IV.15

body.text: tatrāśuddhāvasthā hetvavasthām upādāya yāvat prayogād aśuddhaśuddhāvasthā

children.translated_text: Mvbh 57
is that of the learners; the purified state is that of the non-learners

body.translated_text: Therein, the impure state extends up to the state of cause and application; the impure-pure state
The ordering of persons is to be understood accordingly

body.translated_text: Therefore, from the divisions of state, the ordering of persons is to be understood accordingly—“this one is in the lineage,” “this one has descended,” and so on; the states have been stated
3. Attainment of fruits
What is the attainment of fruits?

children.translated_text: Vesselhood is called maturation; power, because of mastery over that—IV.16

children.text: rucir vṛddhir viśuddhiś ca phalam etad yathākramaṃ /
children.translated_text: Taste, increase, and purification—this is the fruit, in due order,

body.text: bhājanatvaṃ yaḥ kuśalānukūlo vipākaḥ / balaṃ yā bhājanatvādhipatyāt kuśalasyādhimātratā / rucir yā pūrvābhyāsāt kuśalaruciḥ / vṛddhir yā pratyutpanne kuśaladharmābhyāsāt kuśalamūlaparipuṣṭiḥ / viśuddhir yad āvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ / etad yathākramaṃ phalaṃ pañcavidhaṃ veditavyam / vipākaphalam adhipatiphalan niṣyandaphalaṃ puruṣakāraphalaṃ visaṃyogaphalañ ca /
body.translated_text: Vesselhood is that maturation which is favorable to the wholesome; power is the greater measure of the wholesome due to the mastery that comes from vesselhood; taste is the taste for the wholesome due to former practice; increase is the fostering of the wholesome roots due to practice of wholesome dharmas arisen in the present; purification is the removal of the coverings; this fivefold fruit, in due order, is to be understood as maturation-fruit, mastery-fruit, outflow-fruit, fruit of personal effort, and separation-fruit,

children.text: uttarottaram ādyañ ca tadabhyāsāt samāptitaḥ // IV.17
children.translated_text: The first and each successive [fruit] up to completion, due to practice of that, successively—IV.17

children.text:
ānukūlyād vipakṣāc ca visaṃyogād viśeṣataḥ /
uttarānuttaratvāc ca phalam anyat samāsataḥ // IV.18
children.translated_text: Because of favorableness, and because of the adversary, on account of disjunction, and especially because of distinction; and because of higher and unsurpassed, the fruit is otherwise (i.e., is to be classified differently) in brief—IV.18

body.text: uttarottaraphalaṃ gotrāc cittotpāda ity evamādi paraṃparayā veditavyaṃ / ādiphalaṃ prathamato lokottaradharmapratilambhaḥ / abhyāsaphalaṃ tasmāt pareṇa śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ / samāptiphalam aśaikṣādharmāḥ / ānukūlyaphalam upaniṣadbhāvenottarottaraphalam eva veditavyaṃ / vipakṣaphalaṃ prahāṇamārgo yad evādiphalaṃ / pratipakṣo 'bhipretaḥ / visaṃyogaphalaṃ nirodhasākṣātkriyā abhyāsaphalaṃ samāptiphalaṃ ca kleśavisaṃyogaḥ

children.translated_text: Mvbh 58

children.text: śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ yathākramaṃ / viśeṣaphalam abhijñādiko guṇaviśeṣaḥ / uttaraphalaṃ bodhisatvabhūmayas tadanyayānottaratvād anuttaraphalaṃ buddhabhūmiḥ / etāni catvāri abhyāsasamāptiphalaprabheda eva etad anyat phalaṃ samāsanirdeśato vyāsatas tv aparimāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: The distinction-fruit is the distinguished quality such as superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>); the higher fruit is the <s>bodhisattva</s> grounds, because of being higher than the other vehicles; and the unsurpassed fruit is the Buddha-ground; these four belong precisely to the subdivision of practice-fruit and completion-fruit—this is that “other” fruit, stated in brief; but in detail it is without limit

body.translated_text: The higher-and-higher fruit, from the <s>gotra</s> (lineage) up to the production of mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>)—and so on—should be understood in succession; the initial fruit is, first, the obtaining of supramundane dharmas; the fruit of practice is, after that, in the learner’s state; the fruit of completion is the non-learner dharmas; the favorableness-fruit is to be understood, in the manner of an upaniṣad (inner ground/propinquity), precisely as the successive higher-and-higher fruit; the adversary-fruit is the path of abandonment—which indeed is the initial fruit—the intended antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>); the disjunction-fruit is the direct realization of cessation, and the disjunction from afflictions is both the fruit of practice and the fruit of completion, for learner and non-learner respectively
Summary-meaning of the cultivation of the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanā</s>)

body.text: tatra pratipakṣabhāvanāyāḥ piṇḍārthaḥ / vyutpattibhāvanā nirlekhabhāvanā parikarmabhāvanā / uttarasamārambhabhāvanā / śliṣṭabhāvanā darśanamārgaśleṣāt / praviṣṭabhāvanā utkṛṣṭabhāvanā ādibhāvanā madhyabhāvanā paryavasānabhāvanā / sottarā bhāvanā niruttarā ca bhāvanā yālambanamanaskāraprāptiviśiṣṭā // avasthānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ / bhavyatāvasthā gotrasthasya / ārambhāvasthā yāvat prayogāt / asuddhāvasthā aśuddhaśuddhāvasthā viśuddhāvasthā / sālaṃkārāvasthā / vyāptyavasthā daśabhūmivyāpanāt / anuttarāvasthā ca // phalānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ saṃgrahataḥ tadviśeṣataḥ pūrvābhyāsataḥn uttarottaranirhārataḥ / uddeśato nirdeśataś ca / tatra saṃgrahataḥ / pañca phalāni / tadviśeṣataḥ śeṣāṇi / pūrvābhyāsataḥ vipākaphalaṃ / uttarottaranirhāratas tadanyāni catvāri / uddeśataḥ uttarottaraphalādīni catvāri nirdeśataḥ ānukūlyaphalādini ṣaṭ / teṣām eva
body.translated_text: There, the gist of the cultivation of the antidote: cultivation by way of derivation (analysis), cultivation by way of eradication of traces (non-inscription), cultivation by way of preparation; cultivation by way of the higher undertaking; conjoined cultivation, because of conjunction with the path of seeing; entered cultivation, excellent cultivation, initial cultivation, middle cultivation, final cultivation; cultivation with higher (sequel), and cultivation without higher (sequel), distinguished by object and by attention and by attainment. The gist of the states: the state of being capable (fit to be guided) is that of one established in <s>gotra</s>; the state of initiation is up to application; the impure state, the impure–pure state, the pure state; the ornamented state; the state of pervasion because of pervading the ten grounds; and the unsurpassed state. The gist of fruits, in summary, as to their distinctions, from prior practice, and by extraction in successive higher stages; by indication (heading) and by detailed statement: therein, in summary, there are five fruits; as to their distinctions, the remaining ones; from prior practice, the maturation-fruit (<s>vipāka-phala</s>); by extraction in successive higher stages, the other four; by indication, the four beginning with the higher-and-higher fruit; by detailed statement, the six beginning with the favorableness-fruit; by the detailed statement of just those four
Mvbh 59
it is to be understood
In the Madhyāntavibhāga, the delineation of the stages, fruits, and states of the cultivation of the antidote is the fourth
