CHAPTER V. Delineation of the Unexcelledness of the Vehicles
[1. The threefold unexcelledness]
Now the unexcelledness of the vehicles is to be stated; that is said

children.text:
ānuttaryaṃ prapattau hi punar ālambane mataṃ /
samudāgama uddiṣṭaṃ /
children.translated_text: Unexcelledness is, to be sure, held with respect to practice, and again with respect to the object; unexcelledness by way of assemblage is taught

body.text: trividham ānuttaryaṃ mahāyāne yenaitad anuttaraṃ yānaṃ pratipattyānuttaryaṃ / ālambanānuttaryaṃ / samudāgamānuttaryañ ca /
body.translated_text: Threefold is the unexcelledness in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>: by which this vehicle is unexcelled—unexcelledness of practice; unexcelledness of object; and unexcelledness of assemblage
2. Unexcelledness of practice
There, the unexcelledness of practice is to be understood from the practice of the ten <s>pāramitās</s>

children.translated_text: Practice, moreover, is sixfold—V.1

body.translated_text: Among those <s>pāramitās</s>,

children.text:
paramātha manaskāre anudharme 'ntavarjane /
viśiṣṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca /
children.translated_text: In the highest (parama) and in attention, in the non-dharma, in the absence of the two extremes; the distinguished and the non-distinguished

body.text: ity eṣā ṣaḍvidhā pratipattir yad uta paramā pratipattiḥ / manaskārapratipattir anudharmapratipattiḥ / antadvayavarjitā pratipattiḥ viśistā pratipattiḥ / aviśiṣṭā ca pratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus this sixfold practice, namely: the highest practice; the attention-practice; the non-dharma-practice; the practice devoid of the two extremes; the distinguished practice; and also the non-distinguished practice
a. The highest practice
Therein,
Mvbh 61

children.translated_text: The highest is twelvefold—V.2
Magnanimity and extensiveness, commitment and imperishableness,

children.text: nairantaryam akṛcchratvaṃ vittatvaṃ ca parigrahaḥ // V.3
children.translated_text: Uninterruptedness and easiness, liberality and acceptance,
Initiation, attainment, outflow, and accomplishment are regarded as the highest

body.text: ity eṣā dvādaśavidhā paramā matā / yad utaudāryaparamatā āyatatvaparamatā adhikāraparamatā akṣayatvaparamatā nairantaryaparamatā akṛcchratvaparamatā / vittatvaparamatā parigrahaparamatā / ārambhaparamatā pratilambhaparamatā niṣyandaparamatā niṣpattiparamatā ca / tatraudāryaparamatā sarvalaukikasaṃpattyanarthitvenotkṛṣṭatayā ca veditavyā / āyatatvaparamatā trikalpāsaṃkhyeyaparibhāvanāt / adhikāraparamatā sarvasatvārthakriyādhikārāt / akṣayatvaparamatā mahābodhipariṇāmanayātyantam aparyādānān nairantaryaparamatātmaparasamatādhimokṣāt sarvasatvadānādibhiḥ pāramitāparipūraṇād akṛcchratvaparamatānumodanāmātreṇa paradānādīnāṃparamitāparipūraṇāt / vittatvaparamatā / gaganagañjasamādhyādibhir dānādiparipūraṇāt parigrahaparamatā nirvikalpajñānaparigṛhītatvāt / ārambhaparamatādhimukticaryābhūmāv adhimātrāyāṃ kṣāntau pratilambhaparamatā prathamāyāṃ bhūmau / niṣyandaparamatā / tadanyāsv aṣṭāsu bhūmiṣu / niṣpattiparamatā daśamyāṃ bhūmau tathāgatyāṃ ca / bodhisatvaniṣpattyā buddhaniṣpattyā ca /
body.translated_text: Thus this twelvefold “highest” is regarded; namely: the highest of magnanimity, the highest of extensiveness, the highest of commitment (authority to act), the highest of imperishableness, the highest of uninterruptedness, the highest of easiness; the highest of abundancy (wealth), the highest of acceptance (appropriation); the highest of initiation, the highest of attainment, the highest of outflow (effusion), and the highest of accomplishment; therein, the highest of magnanimity is to be understood as excellence because of non-desire for all worldly prosperities and because of superiority; the highest of extensiveness, from cultivation through incalculable three eons; the highest of commitment, from the authorization (mandate) to perform the welfare of all beings; the highest of imperishableness, because by dedication to great awakening (<s>mahābodhi-pariṇāmanā</s>) there is absolutely no exhaustion; the highest of uninterruptedness, from the resolve of equality of self and other and from the giving to all beings and the like; the highest of easiness, from fulfillment of the <s>pāramitā</s>s of others such as giving merely by rejoicing; the highest of abundancy (wealth), from the fulfillment of giving and the like by such as the <s>Gaganagañja-samādhi</s>; the highest of acceptance, because it is embraced by non-conceptual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpa-jñāna</s>); the highest of initiation, at the level of practice of resolve (<s>adhimukti-caryā-bhūmi</s>) when patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) is at a surpassing measure; the highest of attainment, on the first ground; the highest of outflow (effusion), on the other eight grounds; the highest of accomplishment, on the tenth ground and at Buddhahood; by the accomplishment of the <s>bodhisattva</s> and by the accomplishment of the Buddha

children.text: tataś ca paramārthena daśa pāramitā matāḥ // V.4
children.translated_text: And from that, in the ultimate sense, the ten <s>pāramitā</s>s are regarded V.4

body.text: yata eṣā dvādaśavidhā paramatā etāsu saṃvidyate / tataḥ paramā

children.translated_text: Mvbh 62

children.text: ity anenārthena daśa pāramitāḥ / katamā daśety ekeṣāṃ tannāmavyutpādanārtham ucyate /

body.translated_text: Since this twelvefold “highest” is included within these, therefore “highest”—in this sense—the ten <s>pāramitā</s>s; which ten?—for some, in order to derive the meaning of their names, it is said,

children.text:
dānaṃ śīlaṃ kṣamā vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñā upāyatā /
praṇidhānaṃ balaṃ jñānam etāḥ pāramitā daśeti // V.5
children.translated_text: Giving (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), skill-in-means (<s>upāyatā</s>), vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), power (<s>bala</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>)—these are the ten <s>pāramitā</s>s V.5

body.translated_text: What is the function of these, each individually?

children.text:
anugraho 'vighātaś ca karma tasya ca marṣaṇaṃ /
guṇavṛddhiś ca sāmarthyam avatāravimocane /
akṣayatvaṃ sadā vṛttir niyataṃ bhogapācane // V.6
children.translated_text: Bestowal of benefit and non-injury is the function of that, and forbearance; increase of qualities, and ability in bringing down and setting forth; inexhaustibility, constant engagement, definiteness in maturing enjoyments V.6

body.text: ity etad āsāṃ karma yathākramaṃ / dānena hi bodhisatvaḥ satvān anugṛhṇāti / śīlenopaghātaṃ pareṣāṃ na karoti / kṣāntyā paraiḥ kṛtam upaghātaṃ marṣayati / vīryeṇa guṇān vardhayati / dhyānena rddhyādibhir āvarjyāvatārayati / prajñayā samyagavavādadānād vimocayati / upāyakauśalyapāramitayā mahābodhipariṇāmanād dānādīn akṣayān karoti / praṇidhānapāramitayānukūlopapattiparigrahāt / sarvajanmasu buddhotpādārāgaṇato dānādiṣu sadā pravartate balapāramitayā pratisaṃkhyānabhāvanābalābhyāṃ niyataṃ dānādiṣu pravartate / vipakṣānabhibhavāt / jñānapāramitayā yathārutadharmasaṃmohāpagamād dānādyādhipateyadharmasaṃbhogañ ca pratyanubhavati / satvāṃś ca paripācayati / uktā paramā pratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus this is their function in due order: by giving, the <s>bodhisattva</s> benefits beings; by morality, he does not inflict injury on others; by patience, he forbears the injury done by others; by vigor, he increases virtues; by meditation, by such as supernormal success (<s>ṛddhi</s>) he draws in and brings down (beings); by wisdom, by imparting right doctrine he frees; by the perfection of skill-in-means, by dedication to great awakening he makes giving and the rest inexhaustible; by the perfection of vow, because of the appropriation of favorable rebirths, from the beginning of the aspiration to produce Buddhahood through all births he is always engaged in giving and the like; by the perfection of power, through the powers of analytical reflection and cultivation he engages definitively in giving and the like, not overcome by adversaries; by the perfection of knowledge, through the removal of delusion regarding scriptural words and meanings he directly experiences both the enjoyment of the lordly dharmas of giving and the rest, and he matures beings; thus the “highest” practice has been stated
b. Practice of attention (<s>manasikāra-pratipatti</s>)
Mvbh 63
What is the practice of attention?

children.text:
yathāprajñaptito dharmamahāyānamanaskriyā /
bodhisatvasya satataṃ prajñayā triprakārayā // V.7
children.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyāna</s> attention to dharmas according to designation, continually by the <s>bodhisattva</s> with the threefold wisdom V.7

body.text: dānādīny adhikṛtya yathāprajñaptānāṃ sūtrādidharmāṇāṃ mahāyāne manasikaraṇam abhīkṣṇaṃ śrutacintābhāvanāmayyā prajñayā manasikārapratipattiḥ / sā triprakārayā prajñayā manasikriyā kaṃ guṇaṃkaroti /
body.translated_text: With respect to giving and the rest, frequent attending in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> to the dharmas such as sūtras, as designated—by the wisdom consisting of hearing, reflection, and cultivation—is the practice of attention; with that threefold wisdom, what benefit does such attending produce?
It serves for the nourishment of the elements, for entry, and for the accomplishment of the aim

body.text: śrutamayyā prajñayā manasikurvato dhātupuṣṭir bhavati / cintāmayyā tasya śrutasyārthaṃ bhāvena praviśati / bhāvanāmayyārthasiddhiṃ prāpnoti bhūmipraveśapariśodhanāt /
body.translated_text: By wisdom derived from hearing, for one who attends, there is nourishment of the elements; by that derived from reflection, he enters into the meaning of what was heard in its reality; by that derived from cultivation, he attains accomplishment of the aim, through purification for entry into the grounds

children.text: saṃyuktā dharmacaritaiḥ sā jñeyā daśabhiḥ punaḥ // V.8
children.translated_text: Conjoined with dharma-conducts, it is again to be known as tenfold V.8

body.text: sā punar manasikārapratipattiḥ / daśabhir dharmacaritaiḥ parigṛhītā veditavyā katamad daśadhā dharmacaritaṃ /
body.translated_text: That practice of attention, moreover, is to be understood as encompassed by ten dharma-conducts; what is the tenfold dharma-conduct?

children.text:
lekhanā pūjanā dānaṃ śravaṇaṃ vācanodgrahaḥ /
prakāśanātha svādhyāyaś cintanā bhāvanā ca tat // V.9
children.translated_text: Writing out, worship, giving, listening, recitation and grasping, promulgation and also self-study, reflection, and cultivation—those V.9

body.text: mahāyānasya lekhanaṃ pūjanaṃ parebhyo dānaṃ pareṇa vācyamānasya śravaṇaṃ / svayaṃ ca vācanaṃ / udgrahaṇaṃ / parebhyo deśanaṃ granthasyārthasya vā svādhyāyanaṃ / cintanaṃ bhāvanañ ca /
body.translated_text: Writing out of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, worship, giving to others, listening when it is being recited by another, one’s own recitation, memorization, teaching to others, self-study of the book or of its meaning, reflection, and cultivation,
Indeed, that dharma-conduct, being tenfold, is a mass of immeasurable merit,
Mvbh 64

body.text: kasmān mahāyāna eva dharmacaritam atyarthaṃ mahāphalan deśyate sūtreṣu na punaḥ śrāvakayāne / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ /
body.translated_text: Why, precisely in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, is the dharma-conduct taught in the sūtras as exceedingly of great fruit, and not in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>? For two reasons,
Because of distinctiveness, and because of inexhaustibility,
In what way because of distinctiveness? In what way because of inexhaustibility?

children.translated_text: Because of benefiting others, and because of non-quiescence—V.10

body.text: parānugrahavṛttitvād viśiṣṭatvaṃ / parinirvāṇe 'py aśamāt / anuparamād akṣayatvaṃ veditavyaṃ / uktā manasikārapratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: Because it functions in benefiting others, there is distinctiveness; and even at <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, because of non-quiescence—because there is no cessation—its inexhaustibility is to be understood; thus the practice of attention (<s>manasikāra-pratipatti</s>) has been stated,
c. Practice of the non-dharma (anudharma-practice)
What is the anudharma-practice?
Un-distractedness and non-perversion-fulfillment—these are the anudharmic [practices],

body.text: ity eṣā dvividhānudharmapratipattiḥ / yad utāvikṣiptā cāviparyāsapariṇatā ca /
body.translated_text: Thus this anudharma-practice is twofold: namely, the un-distracted, and the fulfilled in non-perversion,
Un-distracted-fulfillment

body.text: tatra ṣaḍvidhavikṣepābhāvād avikṣiptā / tatra ṣaḍvidho vikṣepaḥ / prakṛtivikṣepaḥ / bahirdhāvikṣepaḥ / adhyātmavikṣepaḥ nimittavikṣepaḥ dauṣṭhulyavikṣepaḥ manasikāravikṣepaś ca / sa eṣa kiṃlakṣaṇo veditavya ity ata āha /
body.translated_text: Therein, because of the absence of sixfold distraction it is un-distracted; therein, the distraction is sixfold: natural distraction, outward distraction, inward distraction, distraction by sign, distraction by roughness, and distraction by attention; as to what characteristics that has which are to be understood, therefore he says,

children.translated_text: Emergence [from concentration], diffusion with respect to an object, and likewise savoring; sinking-and-excitation arisen from taste—V.11
Esteem and purpose-intention, and egoizing even in attention,
Mvbh 65

children.text: hīnacittaṃca vikṣepaḥ parijñeyo hi dhīmatā // V.12
children.translated_text: And low-mindedness—this distraction is to be known by the wise—V.12

body.text: ity evaṃlakṣaṇaḥ ṣaḍvidho vikṣepo yo bodhisatvena parijñeyaḥ / tatra vyutthānaṃ samādhitaḥ pañcabhir vijñānakāyaiḥ prakṛtivikṣepaḥ viṣaye visāro bahirdhāvikṣepaḥ / samādher āsvādanā layauddhatyaṃ cādhyātmavikṣepaḥ / saṃbhāvanābhisandhiḥ nimittavikṣepaḥ / tan nimittaṃ kṛtvā prayogāt / sāhaṃkāramanaskāratā dauṣṭhulyavikṣepaḥ / dauṣṭhulyavaśenāsmimānasamudācārāt / hīnacittatvaṃ / manasikāravikṣepaḥ hīnayānamanasikārasamudācārāt /
body.translated_text: Thus, with just these characteristics, the sixfold distraction which is to be known by the <s>bodhisattva</s>: therein, emergence from samādhi, by the five consciousness-aggregates, is natural distraction; diffusion with respect to an object is outward distraction; savoring of samādhi, and sinking-and-excitation, are inward distraction; esteem and purpose-intention are distraction by sign—because, making that sign the basis, one applies oneself; egoizing-attention is distraction by roughness—because, under the sway of roughness, there is the rise of the conceit ‘I am’; low-mindedness is distraction by attention—because of the rise of the attention of the <s>Hīnayāna</s>,
Non-perversion-fulfillment

body.text: tatrāviparyāso daśavidhe vastuni veditavyaḥ / yad uta /
body.translated_text: Therein, non-perversion is to be understood with respect to ten things, namely,

children.translated_text: In attention to expression and meaning: non-diffusion with respect to the two marks; regarding impurity and purity, regarding adventitiousness—without fear and without discouragement—V.13

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.text:
saṃyogāt saṃstavāc caiva viyogād apy asaṃstavāt /
arthasatvam asatvañ ca vyañjane so 'viparyayaḥ /] V.14
children.translated_text: Because of conjunction and indeed because of praise, and also because of disjunction and non-praise, the reality and non-reality of meaning—this is non-perversion with respect to expression—V.14

body.text: saṃyoge sati vyañjanānām avicchinnoccāraṇatayā asya cedaṃ nāmeti saṃstavāt sārthakatvaṃ viparyayān nirarthakatvam iti / yad evandarśanaṃ so 'viparyāso vyañjane veditavyaḥ / katham arthe 'viparyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: When there is conjunction, because the expressions are uttered without interruption, ‘this is its name’—because of praise—there is meaningfulness; because of the contrary, meaninglessness; thus whatever is seen right there, that is the non-perversion to be understood with respect to expression; how is there non-perversion with respect to meaning?

children.text:
dvayena pratibhāsatvaṃ tathā cāvidyamānatā j
arthe sa cāviparyāsaḥ sadasatvena varjitaḥ // V.15
children.translated_text: Twofold appearance, and likewise non-existence; with respect to meaning that non-perversion is free from being and non-being—V.15
Mvbh 66

children.text: ca na vidyate / yathā pratibhāsata iti / arthe yad darśanaṃ sa tatrāviparyāsaḥ arthasya satvena varjito grāhyagrāhakābhāvād asatvena varjitaḥ / tatpratibhāsabhrāntisadbhāvāt /
children.translated_text: it does not exist, just as it appears—thus; with respect to meaning, whatever is the seeing there, that is non-perversion therein—free from the being of meaning, because of the absence of grasper and graspable; free from non-being, because of the existence of the illusion-like appearance of that,

children.text:
tajjalpabhāvito jalpamanaskāras tadāśrayaḥ
manaskāre 'viparyāso dvayaprakhyānakāraṇe // V.16
children.translated_text: The chatter-attention fashioned by that chatter, being its support—non-perversion in attention is with respect to the cause of the proclamation of the two—V.16

body.translated_text: It appears as two, as graspable and grasper, due to the arising of that form; and likewise,

body.text: grāhyagrāhakajalpaparibhāvito jalpamanaskāras tasya grāhyagrāhakavikalpasyāśrayo bhavatīty ayaṃ manaskāre 'viparyāsaḥ / katamasmin manaskāre grāhyagrāhakasaṃprakhyānakāraṇe sa hy asau jalpamanaskāro 'bhilāpasaṃjñāparibhāvitatvāt grāhyagrāhakavikalpāśrayo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The chatter-attention fashioned by the chatter of grasper and graspable becomes the support of that conceptualization of grasper and graspable; thus this is non-perversion with respect to attention—namely, in that attention which is the cause of the proclamation of grasper and graspable; for that chatter-attention, being fashioned by what is named speech, is to be understood as the support of the conceptualizations of grasper and graspable,

children.text:
māyādivad asatvañ ca satvaṃ cārthasya tan mataṃ [/]
so 'visāre 'viparyāso bhāvābhāvāvisārataḥ // V.17
children.translated_text: Just as with illusion and the like, non-being; and being also, of meaning—this is their view; in non-diffusion, non-perversion—because of non-diffusion with respect to being and non-being—V.17

body.text: yat tad arthasyāsatvaṃ satvaṃ cānantaram uktaṃ / tan māyādivan mataṃ yathā māyā na hastyādibhāvenāsti na ca naivāsti / tadbhrāntimātrāstitvāt / evam artho 'pi na cāsti yathā saṃprakhyāti grāhyagrāhakatvena na ca naivāsti tadbhrāntimātrāstitvāt / ādiśabdena marīcisvapnodakacandrādayo dṛṣṭāntā yathāyogaṃ veditavyā iti yan māyādyupamārthe darśanād avisāraṃ cetasaḥ paśyati so 'visāre 'viparyāsas tena bhāvābhāvayoś cittasyāvisaraṇāt /
body.translated_text: That which, immediately before, was stated as the non-existence of meaning and its existence—this is held to be like illusion (<s>māyā</s>); just as illusion does not exist in the form of an elephant and the like, nor does it not exist, because there is only the existence of that delusive appearance; so too meaning does not exist as discrimination makes it, as grasper and graspable, nor does it not exist, because there is only the existence of that delusive appearance; by the word “and so on,” the examples of a mirage, a dream, water, the moon, and the like are to be understood as appropriate; therefore, one who, on seeing the meaning likened to illusion and so on, observes the non-diffusion of mind—he, in non-diffusion, is in non-perversion, because of the mind’s non-diffusion regarding being and non-being,
Mvbh 67

children.translated_text: The mere-namedness of everything is for the cessation of all conceptual constructions; non-perversion with regard to the own-characteristic,

body.text: sarvam idaṃ nāmamātraṃ / yad idaṃ cakṣūrūpaṃ yāvan manodharmā iti yaj jñānaṃ sarvavikalpānāṃ pratipakṣeṇa ayaṃ svalakṣaṇe 'viparyāsaḥ / katamasmin svalakṣaṇe /
body.translated_text: All this is mere name—whatever is up to “eye and form” and as far as mental-dharmas; that knowledge, as the counteragent of all conceptual constructions, this is non-perversion with regard to the own-characteristic; with regard to which own-characteristic?

children.translated_text: With regard to the ultimate own-characteristic V.18

body.text: saṃvṛtyā tu nedaṃ nāmamātram iti gṛhyate /
body.translated_text: But conventionally, this is not apprehended as mere name,

children.text:
dharmadhātuvinirmukto yasmād dharmo na vidyate /
sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ tasmāt sa ca tatrāviparyayaḥ // V.19
children.translated_text: Since, when freed from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, no dharma is found; therefore, the general characteristic is the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and there, that is non-perversion V.19

body.text: na hi dharmanairātmyena vinā kaścid dharmo vidyate / tasmād dharmadhātuḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sāmānyaṃ lakṣaṇam iti / yad evaṃjñānam ayaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇe 'viparyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: For indeed, there is no dharma that exists without the non-self of dharmas; therefore, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is the common characteristic of all dharmas; knowledge just thus is non-perversion with regard to the general characteristic,

children.text:
viparyastamanaskārāvihāniparihāṇitaḥ /
tadaśuddhir viśuddhiś ca sa ca tatrāviparyayaḥ // V.20
children.translated_text: From the non-abandonment and diminution by a perverted attention, impurity; and abandonment, purity—and there, that is non-perversion V.20

body.text: viparyastasmanaskārāprahāṇan tasya dharmadhātor aviśuddhis tatprahāṇaṃ viśuddhir iti yad evaṃjñānam ayam aviśuddhau viśuddhau cāviparyāso yathākramaṃ /
body.translated_text: Non-abandonment by perverted attention—there is impurity of that <s>dharmadhātu</s>; its abandonment is purity; thus, knowledge just so is non-perversion with respect to impurity and purity, in due order,

children.text:
dharmadhātor viśuddhatvāt prakṛtyā vyomavat punaḥ /
dvayasyāgantukatvaṃ hi sa ca tatrāviparyayaḥ // V.21
children.translated_text: Because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is pure by nature, like space again; indeed, duality is adventitious—and there, that is non-perversion V.21

body.text: dharmadhātoḥ punar ākāśavat / prakṛtiviśuddhatvāt / dvayam apy etad āgantukam aviśuddhiru viśuddhiś ca paścād iti / yad evaṃjñānam ayam āgantukatve 'viparyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmadhātu</s>, moreover, is like space, because it is naturally pure; and both of these—impurity and purity—are adventitious, the former earlier, the latter later; thus, knowledge just thus is non-perversion concerning adventitiousness,
Mvbh 68

children.text:
saṃkleśaś ca viśuddhiś ca dharmapudgalayor na hi /
asatvāt trāsatāmānau nātaḥ so 'trāviparyayaḥ // V.22
children.translated_text: And defilement and purification do not belong to dharmas or to a person, indeed; because of non-existence, fear and arrogance do not arise—there, that is non-perversion V.22

body.text: na hi pudgalasya saṃkleśo na viśuddhir nāpi dharmasya / yasmān na pudgalo 'sti na dharmo yataś ca na kasyacit saṃkleśo na vyavadānaṃ ato na saṃkleśapakṣe kasyacid dhāniḥ na vyavadānapakse kasyacid viśeṣaḥ / yatas trāso vā syād unnatir vety ayam atrāse 'nunnatau cāviparyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: For there is neither defilement nor purification of a person, nor of a dharma; since there is no person and no dharma, therefore there is no one at all for whom there is defilement or purification; hence, on the side of defilement there is no diminution for anyone, and on the side of purification there is no superiority for anyone; therefore, whether there would be fear or self-exaltation, this is non-perversion here, in the absence of fear and of conceit,
The ten vajra-words

body.text: ete ca daśāviparyāsā daśasu vajrapadeṣu yathākramaṃ yojayitavyāḥ / daśa vajrapadāni / sadasattā aviparyasaḥ / āśrayo māyopamatā avikalpanatā prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ / ākāśopamatā ahīnatā aviśiṣṭatā ca / vajrapadānāṃ śarīravyavasthānaṃ / svabhāvataḥ / ālambanataḥ / avikalpanataḥ / codyaparihārataś ca / tatra svabhāvataḥ trayaḥ svabhāvāḥ / pariniṣpannaparikalpitaparatantrākhyā ādyais tribhiḥ padair yathākramaṃ / ālambanataḥ / ta eva avikalpanato yena ca na vikalpayati nirvikalpena jñānena yac ca na vikalpayati prakṛtiprabhāsvaratāṃ / tad anena jñeyajñānavyavasthānaṃ yathākramaṃ veditavyaṃ / yad uta tribhiḥ svabhāvair avikalpanatayā ca / codyaparihārataḥ / śiṣṭāni padāni tatredaṃ codyaṃ / yady ete parikalpitaparatantralakṣaṇā dharmā na saṃvidyante / katham upalabhyante / atha saṃvidyante dharmāṇāṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā na
body.translated_text: And these ten non-perversions are to be applied, in due order, to the ten <s>vajrapada</s>s; the ten <s>vajrapada</s>s are: existence-and-non-existence, non-perversion; basis, likeness-to-illusion, non-conceptuality, natural luminosity, defilement, purification, likeness-to-space, non-deficiency, and non-distinction; the arrangement of the body of the <s>vajrapada</s>s is by nature, by object, by non-conceptuality, and by way of objection-and-reply; therein, by nature there are three natures, called the perfected, the imagined, and the dependent, in due order with the first three terms; by object, those very ones; by non-conceptuality, both that by which one does not conceptualize—by non-conceptual knowledge—and that which one does not conceptualize—natural luminosity; by this, the arrangement of knowables and knowledge is to be understood in due order, namely, by the three natures and by non-conceptuality; by way of objection-and-reply, the remaining terms; here the objection is this: if dharmas characterized as imagined and dependent are not found, how are they apprehended? But if they are found, then natural luminosity of dharmas is not—
Mvbh 69

body.text: yujyate / tan māyopamatayā pariharati / yathā māyākṛtaṃ na vidyata upalabhyate ca yadi prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā dharmāṇāṃ tat kathaṃ pūrvaṃ saṃkleśaḥ paścād vyavadānaṃ / asya parihāraḥ / saṃkleśavyavadānam ākāśopamatayā veditavyaṃ / yathākāśaṃ prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ saṃkliśyate / vyavadāyate ceti / yady aprameyabuddhotpāde saty aprameyāṇāṃ satvānāṃ kleśāpaśamaḥ / tat kathaṃ na saṃsārasamucchedo na nirvāṇavṛddhir bhavati / tasyāhīnāviśiṣṭatayā parihāraḥ / aprameyatvāt satvadhātor vyavadānapakṣasya ca /
body.translated_text: He raises an objection: “It fits; let him refute it by means of the likeness-to-illusion. Just as what is produced by illusion does not exist and yet is apprehended, if there is the natural luminosity of dharmas (<s>prakṛti-prabhāsvaratā dharmāṇām</s>), then how is there earlier defilement and later purification?” Its rebuttal: defilement and purification are to be understood by the likeness-to-space; just as space, though naturally pure, is said to be defiled and purified, so too here; [Objection:] “If, when an immeasurable arising of Buddhas occurs, there is the pacification of the afflictions of immeasurable beings, then how is there not a cutting off of saṃsāra and not a growth of <s>nirvāṇa</s>?” Its rebuttal is by non-deficiency and non-distinction, because of the immeasurability both of the realm of beings and of the side of purification,
The second is the arrangement of the body [of the <s>vajrapada</s>s],

d. Practice in the avoidance of the two extremes

body.text: antadvayavarjane pratipattiḥ katamā yā ratnakūṭe madhyamā pratipattir upadiṣṭā / kasyāntasya varjanād asau veditavyā /
body.translated_text: What is the practice in the avoidance of the two extremes? That which, in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>, is taught as the middle practice (<s>madhyamā pratipat</s>); by the avoidance of which extreme is that to be understood?

children.translated_text: Separateness and oneness—an extreme—also among heretics and <s>śrāvakas</s>;
The limit of superimposition and of refutation—twofold—concerning person and dharmas—V.23
The limit of contrary and counteragent, termed eternalism and annihilationism;
In defilement and purification of grasper and graspable—twofold and threefold—V.24

vikalpadvayatāntaś ca sa ca saptavidho mataḥ /
bhāvābhāve praśāmye 'tha śamane trāsyantadbhaye // V.25
children.translated_text: And the limit of the duality of conceptual constructions—this is reckoned sevenfold: in the pacifying of being and non-being; then, in the calming, the fear of the frightening extreme—V.25
Mvbh 70

children.text:
grāhyagrāhe 'tha samyaktvamithyātve vyāpṛtau na ca /
ajanmasamakālatve sa vikalpadvayāntatā // V.26
children.translated_text: And, in grasper and graspable, rightness and wrongness—yet not involvement; and in non-arising and co-temporality—this is the limit of the duality of conceptual constructions—V.26

body.text: tatra rūpādibhyaḥ / pṛthaktvam ātmana ity antaḥ / ekatvam ity antaḥ tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipat / yā nātmapratyavekṣā / yāvan na mānavapratyavekṣā ātmadarśane hi jīvas tac charīraṃ / anyo jīvo 'nyac charīram iti bhavati darśanaṃ / nityaṃ rūpam iti tīrthikāntaḥ / anityam iti śrāvakāntaḥ / tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yā rūpādīnāṃ na nityapratyavekṣā nānityapratyavekṣā / ātmeti pudgalasamāropāntaḥ nairātmyam ity apavādāntaḥ prajñaptisato 'py apavādāt / tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yad ātmanairātmyayor madhyaṃ nirvikalpaṃ jñānaṃ / bhūtaṃ cittam iti dharmasamāropāntaḥ abhūtam ity apavādāntaḥ / tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yatra na cittaṃ na cetanā na mano na vijñānaṃ / akuśalādayo dharmāḥ saṃkleśa iti vipakṣāntaḥ / kuśalādayo vyavadānam iti pratipakṣāntas tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yo 'syāntadvayasyānupagamo 'nudāhāro 'pravyāhāraḥ / astīti śāśvatāntas tayor eva pudgaladharmayor nāstīty ucchedāntas tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yad anayor dvayor antayor madhyaṃ / avidyā grāhyā grāhakā cety antaḥ / evaṃ vidyā saṃskārā asaṃskṛtaṃ ca tatpratipakṣaḥ / yāvaj jarāmaraṇaṃ grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ cety antas tannirodho grāhyo grāhako vety anto yena mārgeṇa tan nirudhyate / evaṃ grāhyagrāhakānto

children.translated_text: Mvbh 71

children.text: dvidhā kṛṣṇaśuklapakṣabhedena tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad vidyā cāvidyā cādvayam etad iti vistareṇa vidyāvidyādīnāṃ grāhyagrāhakatvābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: —is twofold, by the division into dark and white sides; for the avoidance of that, the middle practice is: knowledge and ignorance are non-dual—this, at length, because, for knowledge-and-ignorance and the rest, there is the absence of grasper-and-graspable-ness,

body.translated_text: Therein, beginning with form and so on: “Separateness of a self from them”—this is an extreme; “Oneness”—this is an extreme; for the avoidance of that, the middle practice is that which is not a scrutiny of self, up to not even a scrutiny of conceit-as-person; for, in the view of a self, ‘the living being is that body; one thing is the living being, another the body,’ such is the view; “Form is permanent”—this is the heretical extreme; “It is impermanent”—this is the <s>śrāvaka</s>-extreme; for the avoidance of that, the middle practice is that there is neither a scrutiny of permanence nor a scrutiny of impermanence in form and so on; “Self”—this is the limit of superimposition regarding the person; “non-self”—this is the limit of refutation, even to the point of refuting what is posited by conceptual designation; for the avoidance of that, the middle practice is the non-conceptual knowledge which is the middle between self and non-self of person; “Mind is real”—this is the limit of superimposition regarding dharmas; “It is unreal”—this is the limit of refutation; for the avoidance of that, the middle practice is where there is neither mind, nor mentation, nor manas, nor consciousness; “Unwholesome and the like dharmas are defilement”—this is the limit of the contrary; “Wholesome and the like are purification”—this is the limit of the counteragent; for the avoidance of that, the middle practice is the non-approach to, the non-assertion of, and the non-discourse on this pair of extremes; “It exists”—this is the limit of eternalism, concerning those very two, the person and dharmas; “It does not exist”—this is the limit of annihilationism; for the avoidance of that, the middle practice is that which is the middle between these two extremes; “Ignorance is the grasped and the grasper”—thus an extreme; likewise, “knowledge, formations, and the unconditioned” are its counteragent; up to “aging-and-death are the grasped and the grasper”—thus an extreme; “their cessation is the grasped and the grasper”—thus an extreme; and by which path that is brought to cessation; thus the limit of grasper-and-graspable—

body.text: trividhaḥ saṃkleśaḥ / kleśasaṃkleśaḥ / karmasaṃkleśaḥ / janmasaṃkleśaś ca / tatra kleśasaṃkleśas trividhaḥ / dṛṣṭiḥ rāgadveṣamohanimittaṃ punarbhavapraṇidhānaṃ ca / yasya pratipakṣo jñānaśūnyatā jñānānimittaṃ jñānāpraṇihitaṃ ca / karmasaṃkleśaḥ / śubhāśubhakarmābhisaṃskāraḥ yasya pratipakṣo jñānānabhisaṃskāraḥ / janmasaṃkleśaḥ / punarbhavajātiḥ jātasya cittacaittānāṃ pratikṣaṇotpādaḥ / punarbhavaprabandhaś ca yasya pratipakṣo jñānājātiḥ jñānānutpādo jñānāsvabhāvatā ca / etasya trividhasya saṃkleśasyāpagamo vyavadānaṃ / tatra jñānaśūnyatādibhiḥ / jñeyaśūnyatādayo dharmā etena trividhena saṃkleśena yathāyogaṃ yāvan na śūnyatādayaḥ kriyante / prakṛtyaiva śūnyatādayo dharmadhātoḥ prakṛtyasaṃkliṣṭatvāt tena yadi dharmadhātuḥ saṃkliśyate vā viśudhyate veti kalpayaty ayam antaḥ / prakṛtyasaṃkliṣṭasya saṃkleśaviśuddhyabhāvād etasyāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ / madhyamā pratipat / yan na śūnyatayā dharmāñ chūnyāṃ karoti / api tu dharmā eva śūnyā ity evamādi /
body.translated_text: There are three kinds of entanglement (saṃkleśa): defilement-entanglement, action-entanglement, and birth-entanglement; therein, defilement-entanglement is threefold: view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), intention toward renewed existence on the basis of the signs of lust, hatred, and delusion, whose antidotes are knowledge-emptiness, knowledge-signless, and knowledge-desireless; action-entanglement is the formation of wholesome and unwholesome actions, whose antidote is the non-construction by knowledge; birth-entanglement is the birth of renewed existence, the momentary arising of mind and mental factors in one who has been born, and also the continuous series of renewed existence, whose antidotes are knowledge-non-birth, knowledge-non-arising, and the state of being of the nature of knowledge; the removal of this threefold entanglement is purification; therein, by knowledge-emptiness and the rest, the dharmas such as knowable-emptiness and the like are not, by means of this threefold entanglement, made into emptiness and so on as applicable—for emptiness and the like are by nature [already such], because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is by nature unentangled; therefore, if one imagines that the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is either entangled or purified, this is the extreme; because, for that whose nature is unentangled, there is no entanglement and no purification; for the sake of avoiding this extreme, the middle practice (<s>madhyamā pratipat</s>): which does not, by means of emptiness, make dharmas empty, but rather, “the dharmas themselves are empty,” and so forth,

body.text: aparaḥ saptavidho vikalpadvayāntas tad yathā bhāve 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ/ abhāve 'pi pudgalo 'sti yasya vināśāya śūnyatā

children.translated_text: Mvbh 72

children.text: nairātmyam api vā nāstīti kalpanāt / tad etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārtham iyaṃ madhyamā pratipat / na khalu pudgalavināśāya śūnyatā api tu śūnyataiva śūnyā pūrvāntaśūnyatā / aparāntaśūnyatā ity evamādivistaraḥ /
children.translated_text: or else non-self (<s>nairātmyam</s>) does not exist”—thus by such conceptualizing; therefore, for the sake of avoiding this limit of the duality of conceptual construction, this is the middle practice: it is not at all that emptiness is for the annihilation of the person; rather, emptiness itself is empty—emptiness of the prior extreme, emptiness of the later extreme, and so on in detail,

body.translated_text: Another, the sevenfold limit of the duality of conceptual construction is as follows: even when there is being, there is conceptual construction—an extreme; even when there is non-being, “still a person (<s>pudgala</s>) exists, for whose annihilation emptiness,

body.text: śāmye 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ / śamane 'pi vikalpo 'nataḥ praheyaprahāṇakalpanayā śūnyatāyās trasanād etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārtham ākāśadṛṣṭāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Even in pacification there is conceptual construction—an extreme; even with pacifying there is conceptual construction—an extreme—through the conceptualizing of what is to be abandoned and its abandoning, and through fear with respect to emptiness; for the sake of avoiding this limit of the duality of conceptual construction, there is the illustration of space,

body.text: trāsye 'pi vikalpo 'ntas tataś ca trāsyād bhaye 'pi parikalpitarūpāditrasanāt (/) duḥkhabhīrutayā etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ citrakaradṛṣṭāntaḥ / pūrvako dṛṣṭāntaḥ śrāvakān ārabhyāyaṃ tu bodhisatvān /
body.translated_text: Even in fear there is conceptual construction—an extreme; and then, because there is fear of forms and the like that are merely imagined, through fear itself and through terror of suffering, for the sake of avoiding this limit of the duality of conceptual construction, there is the illustration of the painter; the earlier illustration was for the <s>śrāvaka</s>s, but this one is for the <s>bodhisattva</s>s,

body.text: grāhye 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ grāhake 'pi etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ māyākāradṛṣṭāntaḥ / vijñaptimātrajñānakṛtaṃ hy arthābhāvajñānaṃ / tac cārthābhāvajñānaṃ / tad eva vijñaptimātrajñānaṃ nivartayati / arthābhāve vijñaptyasaṃbhavād ity etad atra sādharmyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Even with respect to the grasped there is conceptual construction—an extreme; and also with respect to the grasper; for the sake of avoiding this limit of the duality of conceptual construction, there is the illustration of the magician; for the knowledge of mere representation (<s>vijñapti-mātra</s>) produces the knowledge of the absence of an external object, and that very knowledge of the absence of an external object turns back that knowledge of mere representation; since, when there is no external object, representation cannot obtain—this is the similarity here,

body.text: samyaktve 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ mithyātve 'pi bhūtapratyavekṣāṃ samyaktvena kalpayato mithyātvena vā etasyāntadvayasya parivarjanārthaṃ / kāṣṭhadvayāgnidṛṣṭāntaḥ / yathākāṣṭhadvayād

children.translated_text: Mvbh 73

children.text: anagnilakṣaṇād agnir jāyate / jātaś ca tad eva kāṣṭhadvayaṃ dahaty evam asamyaktvalakṣaṇāyā yathābhūtapratyavekṣāyāḥ samyaktvalakṣaṇam āryaṃ prajñendriyaṃ jāyate jātaṃ ca tām eva bhūtapratyavekṣāṃ vibhāvayatīty etad atra sādharmyaṃ na cāsamyaktvalakṣaṇāpi bhūtapratyavekṣā mithyātvalakṣaṇā samyaktvānukūlyāt /
children.translated_text: Just as from two sticks, which are characterized as not-fire, fire arises, and when arisen it burns those very two sticks, so too from true examination of reality, characterized as not-rightness, there arises rightness, the noble faculty of wisdom (<s>ārya prajñendriya</s>), and when arisen it illuminates that very true examination of reality—this is the similarity here; nor indeed is true examination of reality, even when characterized as not-rightness, to be called wrongness, because it conduces to rightness,

body.translated_text: Even in rightness there is conceptual construction—an extreme; and even in wrongness, for one who conceptualizes true examination of reality as rightness or as wrongness; for the sake of avoiding this pair of extremes, there is the illustration of the fire from two sticks,

body.text: vyāpṛtāv api vikalpo 'ntaḥ / avyāpṛtāv api jñānasya buddhipūrvāṃ kriyāṃ niḥsāmarthyaṃ vā kalpayataḥ / etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ / tailapradyotadṛṣṭāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Even in involvement there is conceptual construction—an extreme; and even in non-involvement, for one who conceptualizes that knowledge either performs an activity preceded by intellection or is powerless; for the sake of avoiding this limit of the duality of conceptual construction, there is the illustration of the oil-lamp,

body.text: ajanmatve 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ samakālatve 'pi yadi pratipakṣasyānutpattiṃ vā kalpayati saṃkleśasyaiva vā dīrghakālatvam etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ dvitīyas tailapradyotadṛṣṭāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Even in non-arising there is conceptual construction—an extreme; and even in co-temporality, if one conceptualizes either the non-arising of the antidote or the long duration of only the entanglement; for the sake of avoiding this limit of the duality of conceptual construction, there is a second illustration of the oil-lamp,
The practice in the avoidance of the two extremes has been stated,
e. Distinguished and undistinguished practice
There is both a distinguished and an undistinguished practice; which?

body.text: viśiṣṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca jñeyā daśasu bhūmiṣu /
body.translated_text: Both the distinguished and the undistinguished are to be known in the ten <s>bhūmi</s>s

body.text: yasyāṃ bhūmau yā pāramitātiriktatarā sā tatra viśiṣṭā sarvāsu ca sarvatra samudāgacchatīty aviśiṣṭā /
body.translated_text: On whatever <s>bhūmi</s> the perfection (<s>pāramitā</s>) that is more exceptional than the rest is found, there it is distinguished; and, as it appears everywhere among all of them, it is undistinguished,
The unsurpassed practice has been stated,
3. Unsurpassed support (ālambana)
The unsurpassed support—what is it?

children.translated_text: Establishment, and likewise the element (<s>dhātu</s>), the sustaining of the attainable and the means of attainment, V.27
Fixing, predominance, and bearing; penetration, extensiveness,
Mvbh 74

children.text: pragamaḥ praśaṭhatvaṃ ca prakarṣālambanaṃ mataṃ // V.28
children.translated_text: Advance and firmness—this is taught as the superior support, V.28

body.text: ity etat / dvādaśavidham ālambanaṃ / yad uta dharmaprajñaptivyavasthānālambanaṃ dharmadhātvālambanaṃ sādhyālambanaṃ sādhanālambanaṃ / dhāraṇālambanaṃ avadhāraṇālambanaṃ / pradhāraṇālambanaṃ / prativedhālambanaṃ / pratānatālambanaṃ / pragamālambanaṃ / praśaṭhatvālambanaṃ prakarṣālambanaṃ ca / tatra prathamaṃ ye pāramitādayo dharmā vyavasthāpyante / dvitīyan tathatā tṛtīyacaturthe te eva yathākramaṃ dharmadhātuprativedhena pāramitādidharmādhigamāt / pañcamaṃ śrutamayajñānālambanaṃ / ṣaṣṭhaṃ / cintāmayasyāvagamya dhāraṇāt / saptamaṃ bhāvanāmayasya pratyātmaṃ dhāraṇāt / aṣṭamaṃ prathamāyāṃ bhūmau darśanamārgasya / navamaṃ bhāvanāmārgasya yāvat saptamyāṃ bhūmau / daśamaṃ tatraiva laukikalokottarasya mārgasya / prakāraśo dharmādhigamāt / ekādaśam aṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau dvādaśaṃ navamyādibhūmitraye tad eva hi prathamadvayaṃ / tasyān tasyām avasthāyāṃ tattadālambanaṃ nāma labhate /
body.translated_text: Thus, this is the twelvefold support: namely, the support of establishment by conceptual designation of dharmas (<s>dharmaprajñapti-vyavasthāna-ālambana</s>); the support of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>; the support of the attainable; the support of the means of attainment; the support of bearing (dhāraṇā); the support of fixing (avadhāraṇa); the support of predominance (pradhāraṇā); the support of penetration (prativedha); the support of extensiveness (pratānatā); the support of advance (pragama); the support of firmness (praśaṭhatva); and the support of superiority (prakarṣa). Therein, first, the dharmas beginning with the <s>pāramitā</s>s are established; second, suchness (<s>tathatā</s>); third and fourth, those very ones in due order, through penetration of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> by way of the attainment of the dharmas beginning with the <s>pāramitā</s>; the fifth is the support of hearing-born knowledge (<s>śrutamaya-jñāna</s>); the sixth, of reflection-born (cintāmaya), since, being apprehended, it is borne; the seventh, of cultivation-born (bhāvanāmaya), since it is borne individually; the eighth, of the path of seeing on the first <s>bhūmi</s>; the ninth, of the path of cultivation up to the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>; the tenth, there itself, of the path that is mundane-and-transmundane, since dharmas are attained by way of modes; the eleventh, on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s>; the twelfth, on the triad of <s>bhūmi</s>s beginning with the ninth; for the very first two are there: in this or that stage, that particular support obtains the name ‘such-and-such support,’
The support has been stated,
4. Unsurpassed emergence (samudāgama)
What is the emergence?

children.text:
avaikalyāpratikṣepo 'vikṣepaś ca prapūraṇā /
samutpādo nirūḍhiś ca karmaṇyatvāpratiṣṭhitā /

children.translated_text: Non-deficiency and non-rejection, and non-distraction, and fulfillment; arising, and maturation, and fitness-for-action, and non-establishment; non-obstruction—its non-relaxation is the emergence, V.29

children.translated_text: Non-rejection of the Great Vehicle—emergence of resolute faith (<s>adhimukti-samudāgama</s>); non-distraction toward the Lesser Vehicle—emergence of the thought of awakening (<s>cittotpāda-samudāgama</s>); fulfillment of the <s>pāramitā</s>s—emergence of practice; arising of the noble path—emergence of entry into certainty (<s>niyāma-avakrānti-samudāgama</s>); maturation of wholesome roots—emergence of maturation of beings, through long-time familiarization; fitness of mind for action—emergence of purification of buddha-field; non-establishment in saṃsāra and <s>nirvāṇa</s>—emergence of the obtaining of prediction on the irreversible <s>bhūmi</s>, because there is no turning back from saṃsāra and <s>nirvāṇa</s>; non-obstruction—emergence of the Buddha-<s>bhūmi</s>; and its non-relaxation—emergence of the vision of awakening,

body.translated_text: This tenfold emergence is as follows: therein, non-deficiency of conditions—emergence of lineage (<s>gotra-samudāgama</s>);

body.text: madhyamāpratipatprakāśanāt madhyāntavibhāgam apy etan madhyasyāntayoś ca prakāśanāt / ādyaparavarjitasya madhyasya vā /
body.translated_text: Because it discloses the middle practice (<s>madhyamā pratipat</s>), it is also the discrimination of the middle and the extremes (<s>madhyānta-vibhāga</s>), by its disclosure of the middle and the ends of the middle; or, of the middle that is free from the first and the last,
And moreover it has a meaning whose essence is hidden,
Because it is beyond the reach of dialectics and, in due order, unassailable by opponents,
And it has great import,
Because it is the foundation for oneself and for others,
It concerns all meanings,
Because it is the foundation of the three vehicles,

children.translated_text: It drives away all misfortunes, V.30

body.translated_text: The gist of the unsurpassed: in brief, the unsurpassed is threefold—practice, the basis of practice, and the fruit of practice; and that practice is such as is supreme; by which

body.translated_text: The gist in brief of the non-perversions: by non-perversion with respect to expression he counteracts the sign of <s>śamatha</s> (calm-abiding), by non-perversion with respect to meaning he counteracts the sign of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), by non-perversion with respect to attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) he avoids the cause of perversion, by non-perversion with respect to non-scattering (<s>avisāra</s>) he makes that sign well-grasped, by non-perversion with respect to particular characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) he cultivates the non-conceptual path by its antidote, by non-perversion with respect to general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) he counteracts the nature of turbidity (obscuration), by non-perversion with respect to attention that takes impurity and purity he knows the state of abandonment and non-abandonment of its coverings (obstructions), by non-perversion with respect to their being adventitious he knows, as it really is, defilement and purification, and here, by non-perversion with respect to non-depression and non-elevation, he proceeds into the unobstructed
